sections.title: Judges, gates, and YOLO mode
sections.summary: How Ostra makes model decisions with ten judge calls, stops for the user at 14 kinds of gate, answers gates itself under YOLO mode, and applies exact review fixes with autofix.
sections.body:
## Why the engine has judges, gates, and YOLO mode

The Ostra planner is plain code. It cannot settle some questions with a fixed rule: the category of a request, the completeness of research, or the meaning of a typed answer. The pipeline also stops for the user at set points, and it must continue when no user is present. This page explains the parts that solve these problems.

- **Judges:** ten model calls. Each call returns JSON for one decision.
- **Gates:** pending questions for the user. Each question type has its own payload kind.
- **YOLO mode:** a session switch that makes the engine answer gates.
- **Judge prompts:** the files in `assets/judges`.
- **Autofix:** an exact text edit of review findings, with no model call.

The model decides only inside a judge call. The header of [`judge.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/judge.rs) states that judge calls are the only places where a model makes an orchestration decision. The engine then performs the result. [Sessions and the pipeline](sessions-and-pipeline.md) owns the planner and the loop caps. [Engine runner](engine-runner.md) owns the runner that performs each step.

## The ten judges

A judge is one model call that returns JSON for one orchestration decision. The enum `JudgeKind` in [`event.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/event.rs) lists the ten judges. Each judge has a prompt file in `assets/judges` that carries the name from `JudgeKind::as_str()`.

| `JudgeKind` | Prompt file | The planner starts it when | `subject` | Result type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Classify` | `classify.md` | The session has no category and no classify decision. | none | `ClassifyOut` |
| `Sufficiency` | `sufficiency.md` | Research tasks ended with `Not covered` items that no decision covered, and fewer than 3 rounds ran. | The task indexes, joined with commas | `SufficiencyOut` |
| `Track` | `track.md` | An `IMPLEMENT` session finished research and has no track. | none | `TrackOut` |
| `Stakes` | `stakes.md` | A full-track session has an approved spec of the current version and has no stakes. | none | `StakesOut` |
| `RouteAnswer` | `route-answer.md` | An answer with text waits, or the user added context to a running session. | A gate ID, or `amendment:N` | `RouteAnswerOut` |
| `Feedback` | `feedback.md` | A feedback round after the implementation review has no route. | The round index | `FeedbackOut` |
| `Rescue` | `rescue.md` | An agent returned `STUCK`. | The execution ID | `RescueOut` |
| `ResolveReview` | `resolve-review.md` | A review loop reaches its budget in a YOLO session. | `phase:N` or `phase:N:tests` | `ResolveReviewOut` |
| `YoloAnswer` | `yolo-answer.md` | A YOLO session has an open gate that needs judgment. | The gate ID | `YoloAnswerOut` |
| `Completion` | `completion.md` | All work ended and no report exists. | none | `CompletionOut` |

The name has two forms. Events, the API, and the generated TypeScript type use snake_case: `route_answer`, `resolve_review`, `yolo_answer`. The prompt file and the `judge_prompt` lookup use kebab-case: `route-answer`, `resolve-review`, `yolo-answer`.

### What the engine does with each result

The fold applies a decision in `SessionState::on_decision` in [`state.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs). These rules show the effect of each judge:

- **Classify:** sets the category, the projects in scope, the first research tasks, the `tests` and `docs` opt-ins, and the session title. `clean_title` cuts the title to 60 characters (`TITLE_CHARS`).
- **Sufficiency:** each item with `needed: true` becomes a research task. The engine skips a task that matches a running or queued task by project and text. After 3 rounds (`SUFFICIENCY_ROUNDS`) the engine goes on with the research it has.
- **Track:** sets `light` or `full`. The light track skips the spec, the fact-check, and the plan.
- **Stakes:** `low` skips the plan stage. The engine creates one inline phase for each project in scope only when the stakes are `low` and the category is `Implement` (`SessionState::on_decision`). This condition covers every case, because the planner starts the `Stakes` judge only for an `IMPLEMENT` session on the full track. No session of another category gets a stakes value. `medium` and `high` run the plan stage.
- **Rescue:** `explore` queues one research task and re-runs the agent with the findings. `rerun` re-runs the agent at once. It uses `fact` when `fact` is present, and it uses `reason` only when `fact` is absent or null. An empty `fact` string does not fall back to `reason`. The code is `out.fact.as_deref().unwrap_or(&out.reason)` in `state.rs`. `gate` opens a `stuck` gate.
- **ResolveReview:** see [The review loop under YOLO](#the-review-loop-under-yolo).
- **RouteAnswer and Feedback:** see [How a typed answer reaches an agent](#how-a-typed-answer-reaches-an-agent).
- **Completion:** stores `report_markdown`. The planner then writes it as the completion report. `YoloAnswer` has no effect in the fold, because the YOLO path reads its result directly.

## How one judge call runs

The planner starts a judge call with `Step::Judge { judge, subject }`. The step key is `judge:<name>:<subject>`. The driver keeps one in-flight step for each key, so the planner cannot start the same judge call twice at the same time.

### Judge call sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Planner
    participant Runner
    participant Services
    participant Provider
    participant Log as EventLog
    participant State
    Planner->>Runner: Step Judge
    Runner->>Runner: judge_input and output_schema
    Runner->>Services: judge with route, system, user, schema, Low
    Services->>Provider: structured call with the forced decide tool
    Provider-->>Services: value and usage
    Services-->>Runner: value and usage
    Runner->>Runner: validate against the result type
    Runner->>Log: append DecisionMade
    Log->>State: apply and on_decision
    State-->>Planner: next planner pass reads the decision
```

These steps run in `perform_judge` and `Inner::call_judge` in [`runner.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs):

1. `perform_judge` takes a snapshot of the session state.
2. `judge_input` builds the user message and a short `input_summary`. `output_schema(kind, None)` builds the JSON schema.
3. `call_judge` loads the system prompt with `factory.judge_prompt(kind.as_str())`.
4. `call_judge` resolves the model route with the key `judge` (`JUDGE_ROUTE`), tier `Advanced`, and effort `Low`.
5. `Services::judge` calls `ostra_providers::structured`. The call forces a `decide` tool whose input must match the schema.
6. `call_judge` adds the cost of the call to the judge cost of the session.
7. `call_judge` parses the value into the result type. `Feedback` also needs at least one target. `YoloAnswer` always passes here, and a later check validates it.
8. `call_judge` appends `DecisionMade`. The fold then applies the decision.

A judge call does not take an execution slot, because `perform_judge` never calls `acquire_slot`. Read [Engine runner](engine-runner.md) for the slot limit. Read [Model providers, tiers, and cost](providers-and-cost.md) for the route and tier rules.

### What happens when a judge call fails

This page owns the judge retry rule. The code is in `Inner::call_judge`.

- **The call fails or the value does not match the schema:** `call_judge` makes 3 attempts. It sleeps 500 ms times (attempt + 1) after each failed attempt, including the third. The waits are 500, 1000, and 1500 ms. The last wait comes before the error returns.
- **All 3 attempts fail:** the runner appends `SessionFailed` with the text `The <judge> judge call failed: <error>. Check that the judge route has a provider with a working API key.`
- **The `Completion` judge fails 3 times:** the runner does not fail the session. It writes a fallback decision with the `input_summary` `Fallback after a failed judge call`. The report starts with `# Session complete` and lists the session state without prose.
- **A prompt file or a route is missing:** `call_judge` returns `EngineError::Invalid` at once, before the first attempt. The runner treats it like a failed call.
- **The session is paused:** the planner starts no judge step and no YOLO answer, because `flows` returns first for a paused session.
- **The server restarts:** the log already holds each stored decision. The fold replays the stored output and never calls the judge again for it.

### Judge cost

The runner adds the cost of each judge call to a per-session total. The session list and `view::summary` include this total in the session cost. The budget guard does not include it, because `SessionState::spent_usd` sums only the cost of executions. Judge calls therefore never trigger the `budget_reached` gate.

## What each judge receives

`judge_input(state, kind, subject, projects)` in [`judge_input.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/judge_input.rs) returns two strings. The first is the user message. The second is the summary that the engine stores as `input_summary` and that the console shows as the basis of a decision.

| Judge | The user message holds | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Classify` | The request with attached files and uploads, the New task toggles (`tests`, `docs`, `yolo`), the pinned projects, and each project with path, stack, and module-map areas. An uninitialized project carries a note that no pipeline task can target it. | `Request:` and the first line |
| `Sufficiency` | The request, each finished research task with scope, findings, and document path, the `Not covered` items of the tasks in `subject`, and the project keys the judge can target. | Count of items and documents |
| `Stakes` | The request, the spec counts and summary, an excerpt of the spec, and the projects in scope. | `Approved spec and request` |
| `Track` | The request, the projects in scope, and every research document with an excerpt. | `Research for:` and the first line |
| `Feedback` | The request, the track, the scope, the spec excerpt or a note that no spec exists, the phases with report paths, the research, the kept notes, and the feedback text. | `Feedback:` and the first line |
| `RouteAnswer` | The request, the category, track, and scope, the research, the spec summary, the plan phases, the kept notes, and the gate. For a gate with questions: each question, its options numbered as the user saw them, and the answer. For an added context: the text, the delivery mode, and the work that Ostra stopped. | `Answer:` or `Added context:` and the first line |
| `Rescue` | The request, the stuck agent, project, and phase, the diagnostic and the need word for word, and the earlier rescue actions with their reasons. | `STUCK:` and the need |
| `ResolveReview` | The phase, the pass count, the resolution rounds, the open findings, an excerpt of the review ledger, and an excerpt of the phase file. | `Open findings and the review ledger` |
| `YoloAnswer` | The request, the gate title and explanation, the gate payload as JSON, and an extra block for three gate kinds: research findings for `open_questions`, the spec excerpt for `spec_approval`, the plan excerpt for `plan_approval`. | The gate title |
| `Completion` | The request, category, YOLO flag, track, feedback rounds, research, spec, plan or stakes, each phase with its status, the closing stages for each project, the gates that YOLO answered, and the notes. | `Session state at completion` |

### Input limits

The excerpt limits count bytes, not characters.

- `FILE_EXCERPT` is 24,000 bytes for a spec, plan, ledger, or phase file.
- `TRACK_EXCERPT` is 12,000 bytes for each research document that the `Track` judge reads.
- `excerpt_n` cuts a longer file at the limit. If the limit falls inside a multi-byte character, `excerpt_n` backs up to the previous character boundary. The text then ends with `(truncated at N characters)`, where N is the byte limit.
- An unreadable file shows `(could not read <path>)`.
- `first_line` takes the first line of a text. If the line is longer than 160 bytes, `first_line` keeps the first 157 characters and adds `...`. A shorter line stays unchanged.
- For a `review_cap` gate the `RouteAnswer` input lists at most 20 findings.

The `Rescue` prompt mentions recalled lessons. `judge_input` does not add lessons. It adds only the earlier rescue decisions of the session.

## What each judge returns

`output_schema(kind, answer_schema)` in [`judge.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/judge.rs) builds the schema for the forced `decide` call. Every schema requires a `reason`: one or two sentences that the user reads. `reason_of` copies it into the `DecisionMade` event.

| Judge | Required fields |
| --- | --- |
| `classify` | `category` (one of `RESEARCH`, `SPEC`, `PLAN`, `IMPLEMENT`, `VERIFY`, `TEST`, `DOCS`, `PROMPT`, `QUICK_CHANGE`, `QUICK_ANSWER`), `projects`, `explore_tasks`, `opts_in` (`tests`, `docs`), `reason`, `title` |
| `sufficiency` | `items`, `reason`. Each item requires `item`, `needed`, and `reason`. The field `task` is optional and holds an explore task or `null`. |
| `stakes` | `stakes` (`low`, `medium`, `high`), `reason` |
| `track` | `track` (`light`, `full`), `reason` |
| `feedback` | `route` (`requirement_change`, `implementation_detail`), `targets` (at least 1, each with `project` and `instruction`), `items`, `research`, `forget`, `reason` |
| `route_answer` | `route` (`requirement_change`, `implementation_detail`, `stage_choice`), `items`, `research`, `forget`, `reason` |
| `rescue` | `action` (`explore`, `rerun`, `gate`), `reason`. Optional: `explore_task`, `fact` |
| `resolve_review` | `action` (`fix`, `block`), `instructions` (each with `finding` and `instruction`), `reason` |
| `yolo_answer` | `answer` (shaped by the gate, see [YOLO mode](#yolo-mode)), `reason` |
| `completion` | `report_markdown`, `reason` |

The schema for `feedback` offers two routes. The `AnswerRoute` enum has a third value, `stage_choice`, that only `route_answer` offers.

### Answer items

`RouteAnswer` and `Feedback` return `items`. Each `AnswerItem` has four fields:

- `id`: the ID of an open question (`Q1`), or `answer` (`ANSWER_ITEM`) for a gate with one text.
- `disposition`: `deliver`, `remember`, or `discard`. The default is `deliver`.
- `stages`: later stages that also receive the note. The values are `implement`, `tests`, and `docs` (`NoteStage`).
- `note`: a self-contained instruction for those stages.

| Disposition | Meaning | What the engine does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deliver` | The answer settles what the stage asked. | The agent that asked receives the answer. |
| `remember` | The whole answer is about a later stage. | The agent that asked receives a note that the question is removed. The engine keeps the note for the named stages. |
| `discard` | The user told Ostra to ignore the answer. | The agent that asked receives a note to remove the question. Nothing is kept. The gate answer stays in the log. |

A model can split one answer into parts. `item_for` merges the parts of one ID. The result is `deliver` if any part delivers, else `remember` if any part remembers, else `discard`. An answer that the judge did not name is delivered. On a gate with one text, `parts_for` treats every item as an item for that text.

### Notes, research, and forget

- **Notes:** the fold stores each remembered part as a `UserNote` with the ID `N1`, `N2`, and so on. Later judge inputs list the notes that are not forgotten.
- **Forget:** `forget` lists note IDs that the answer takes back or replaces. A forgotten note stays in the log and reaches no agent.
- **Research:** `research` lists tasks that run before the engine applies the answer. `queue_research` keeps at most 3 tasks (`MAX_ANSWER_RESEARCH`) and skips empty tasks. A task for an unknown project goes to the primary project.
- **Route:** at a phase gate, a delivered `requirement_change` stops the phase, writes the answer into the spec, and plans again (Rule D10). At the spec gates, every delivered answer goes into the spec, whatever the route. Read [Sessions and the pipeline](sessions-and-pipeline.md) for the spec loop.

## How a decision is stored and overridden

The event `DecisionMade { id, judge, subject, input_summary, output, reason }` stores each decision. The fold keeps it in `SessionState.decisions` as a `DecisionRecord`. The runner also writes it to the decisions table. `DecisionView` in the API adds `overridden`, `can_override`, and `at`.

The user can replace a decision with `POST /api/decisions/{id}/override`. The body is `OverrideDecision { output, reason }`. `Engine::override_decision` runs these checks in order:

1. The decision must exist.
2. `can_override` must return true.
3. The output must parse into the result type of the judge. Only `Classify`, `Stakes`, `Track`, and `Sufficiency` accept an override.
4. The runner marks the decision as overridden in the database.
5. The runner appends `DecisionOverridden { id, output, reason }`.

The fold replaces the stored output and reason, sets `overridden`, and applies the decision again. The original `DecisionMade` event stays in the log.

### When an override is still possible

`SessionState::can_override` answers the question. The override stops being possible when work that depends on the decision starts.

| Judge | The override works until |
| --- | --- |
| `Classify` | A research task starts or a phase does its first work pass. |
| `Sufficiency` | A spec run starts. |
| `Track` | A spec run starts or a phase starts. |
| `Stakes` | A plan run starts or a phase starts. |
| Every other judge | Never possible. |

An ended session never accepts an override. These errors can come back:

- `Work that depends on this decision has already started, so it can no longer be overridden.`
- `The override does not match the decision's output shape.`

The effects differ by judge. A `Stakes` override clears the phases and builds them again. A `Sufficiency` override removes the research tasks that the old decision queued and did not start, then queues the new ones. A `Classify` override applies the classification again.

### Where the user sees decisions

The session screen has a `Decisions` tab. `DecisionsPanel` in [`SidePanels.tsx`](web/src/screens/session/SidePanels.tsx) shows each decision as a sentence: Ostra chose X because Y. The `Override` button opens `OverrideDialog`. The dialog holds the output as editable JSON and a required `Why` field. The dialog refuses invalid JSON and an empty reason before it calls the API.

## Gates and their payloads

A gate is a pending question that the pipeline holds for the user. The engine opens a gate with `GateOpened { id, title, explanation, payload }`. The answer arrives as `GateAnswered { id, source, answer, reason, routed }`. `GatePayload` has 14 variants. Each variant has a `kind_str()` for the API and a `stage()` for the board.

| `kind` | Stage | Answer kind | The gate opens when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open_questions` | `OpenQuestions` | `questions` | The spec or plan has open questions that no gate asked for this version. It opens before the fact-check. |
| `spec_approval` | `SpecApproval` | `approval` | The spec passed its fact-check. The payload lists the LOW findings. |
| `plan_approval` | `PlanApproval` | `approval` | The plan passed its fact-check. The payload lists the phases and the LOW findings. |
| `fact_check_recurring` | `FactCheckSpec` or `FactCheckPlan` | `choice` | The fact-check failed 3 times in a row (`FACTCHECK_RECURRING_LIMIT`), and again after 3 more failures when the user allows more rounds. |
| `review_cap` | `Review` or `TestReview` | `choice` | A review loop used its 3 passes (`REVIEW_CAP`) and YOLO is off. |
| `stuck` | `Rescue` | `choice` | The `Rescue` judge chose `gate`. |
| `phase_blocked` | `Implement` | `choice` | A phase ended blocked, the engine announced it, and YOLO is off. |
| `closing_gate` | `ClosingGate` | `closing` | All phases of a project passed, and the request did not already decide tests and docs. |
| `permission` | `Implement` | `permission` | The policy returned `ask` for a tool call. |
| `harness_failure` | `Implement` | `choice` | A harness executor failed to start or is not logged in. |
| `skill_approval` | `SkillApproval` | `skills` | The init flow proposes skills. |
| `execution_failed` | `Implement` | `choice` | An execution ended in an error after its automatic retry, or the user cancelled it. |
| `implementation_review` | `ImplementationReview` | `choice` | Every phase is built and reviewed. |
| `budget_reached` | `Intake` | `choice` | The session spend reaches the budget plus any raise. No new execution starts. |

The payload carries what the user needs to decide. A `review_cap` payload holds the open findings and the path of the review ledger. A `stuck` payload holds the diagnostic and the need of the agent. An `implementation_review` payload holds the round number, the path of the session context file, the implementer reports, and the blocked phases. [Sessions and the pipeline](sessions-and-pipeline.md) explains the loops that open these gates.

## Gate answers and their checks

`GateAnswer` has six variants. Each gate kind accepts one variant.

| `GateAnswer` | Fields | Accepted by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `questions` | `answers`: a list of `QuestionAnswer { id, question, answer }` | `open_questions` |
| `approval` | `approved`, `feedback` | `spec_approval`, `plan_approval` |
| `choice` | `option`, `text` | the 8 choice gates in the table below |
| `closing` | `items`: a list of `ClosingChoice { project, tests, docs }` | `closing_gate` |
| `permission` | `answer`: `allow-once`, `always-in-workspace`, or `deny` | `permission` |
| `skills` | `decisions`: a list of `SkillDecision { name, disposition }` | `skill_approval` |

The option strings of the choice gates are:

| Gate | Options | The `text` field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fact_check_recurring` | `another-round`, `stop` | Optional guidance for the agent. |
| `review_cap` | `another-pass`, `stop` | Optional instruction for the fix pass. |
| `stuck` | `fact`, `block` | The missing fact. `fact` without text counts as `block`. |
| `phase_blocked` | `retry`, `leave` | Optional instructions for the retry. |
| `harness_failure` | `retry`, `native` | none |
| `execution_failed` | `retry`, `abandon` | none |
| `budget_reached` | `raise`, `stop` | Optional dollar amount. |
| `implementation_review` | `done`, `feedback` | The change to build. Required for `feedback`. |

### The route of an answer

The browser sends `POST /api/gates/{id}/answer` with `AnswerGate { answer }`. `Engine::answer_gate` in [`runner.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs) then runs these checks:

1. The gate must exist and have no answer. Otherwise the error is `This gate was already answered.`
2. `validate_answer` checks the answer.
3. For an approval, `approved: true` needs a fact-check `PASS` on the current version. Otherwise the error is `Approval requires a fact-check PASS on this version.`
4. For the answer `always-in-workspace`, the engine adds the suggested allow rule to the workspace. [Policy engine](policy.md) explains rules.
5. The runner appends `GateAnswered` with `source: user`.
6. For a `permission` gate, the runner sends the answer to the execution that waits for it.

`validate_answer` applies these rules:

- The answer kind must fit the gate kind. The error is `That answer does not fit this gate.`
- Each open question needs a non-empty answer. The error is `Answer Q1 before continuing.`
- A rejected spec or plan needs feedback. The error is `Say what to change.`
- For `implementation_review`, the option `done` is accepted. The option `feedback` with text is accepted. The option `feedback` with no text returns `Say what to change.`
- For `implementation_review`, any other option returns `Answer done, or feedback with what to change.`
- For the other choice gates, `validate_answer` checks only the answer kind. The fold reads the option string.

The file [`web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts`](web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts) mirrors these rules. Its `ANSWER_KIND` table maps each gate kind to its answer kind, and its helpers return an error text before any API call.

### Who answers

`AnswerSource` records who closed the gate:

- **`user`:** a person answered in the console.
- **`yolo`:** the engine answered in a YOLO session. The event carries the reason.
- **`engine`:** the engine answered with no judgment. The code does this only for a `permission` gate. On a server restart, it denies each open ask because the execution ended. When an execution ends, it denies the open asks of that execution.

The comment on `AnswerSource::Engine` also names a closing gate whose stages the request already chose. The planner code opens no gate in that case. It runs the chosen stages at once.

### What happens when

- **Two answers arrive for one gate:** the second API call fails. The fold also ignores a second `GateAnswered` event.
- **The spec changed after the approval gate opened:** the change revokes the gate. A stale `approved: true` does not approve the new version. Any feedback text still goes to the judge.
- **A permission gate is open:** the execution waits for the answer. A denial tells the agent to go on without the call.
- **The server restarts with a permission gate open:** the engine answers `deny` with the reason `The execution that asked ended when the server restarted.`
- **A gate stays open:** the session waits. A push notice tells the user that a step waits, except in a YOLO session.

## Open questions and typed answers

A `Question` has an `id` (`Q1`, `Q2`), the `question` text, a `tag` of at most 12 characters, a list of `options` with `label` and `description`, the index `recommended`, and the flag `multi_select`. The agent lists the recommended option, and the console shows it first.

`Question::display_options` numbers the options from 1. The recommended option gets number 1, and the others keep their order. An out-of-range `recommended` value is ignored. The function `orderedOptions` in `gateAnswers.ts` must give the same order, because a typed answer names options by these numbers. A unit test in [`pipeline.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/pipeline.rs) fixes the Rust order.

### The console form

`QuestionsGate` shows one fieldset for each question. Each option has a radio button, or a checkbox when `multi_select` is true. A last choice, `Other`, opens a text field. The field accepts a free answer. The user can name options by number, combine them, and add requirements. The placeholder is `For example: 1 and 3, plus an audit log`.

`questionsAnswer` builds the answer. It joins the picked labels and the `Other` text into one string with a semicolon and a space. It returns an error for an unanswered question: `Q1 has no answer yet.` An empty `Other` field returns `Q1: write your answer in the Other field.`

### What a typed answer becomes

`Question::is_option_answer` tests whether an answer consists only of option labels. A picked option stays unchanged. A typed answer gets a second part from `Question::answer_in_context`. The second part is a note that the user typed the answer, and a numbered list of the options with labels and descriptions. The agent that reads the answer alone then knows what `1 and 3` means.

The `RouteAnswer` judge sees the same numbered options in its input. The prompt tells the judge to read a typed answer as the combination that it names plus what it adds. The judge must not rewrite the answer.

## How a typed answer reaches an agent

An answer that carries text must reach the right artifact before an agent reads it. For example, the plan agent reads only the spec. An answer that the plan needs must therefore go into the spec first. The code marks such an answer with `routed: true` and lets a judge decide where it goes (Rule J1).

`answer_needs_route(payload, answer)` in `state.rs` returns true for these answers:

- `open_questions` with at least one answer.
- `spec_approval` or `plan_approval` with non-empty feedback.
- `fact_check_recurring` with an option other than `stop` and non-empty text.
- `review_cap` with `another-pass` and text.
- `stuck` with `fact` and text.
- `phase_blocked` with `retry` and text.
- `implementation_review` with `feedback` and text.

A bare choice has one meaning. Examples are an approval, `stop`, `retry`, or a budget raise. The fold applies it at once.

### Answer routing flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["GateAnswered"] --> B{"answer_needs_route"}
    B -->|"no text"| C["Fold applies the answer at once"]
    B -->|"text"| D["Fold holds the answer"]
    D --> E["Judge: RouteAnswer or Feedback"]
    E --> F{"disposition"}
    F -->|"deliver"| G["Agent gets the answer and the route picks the target"]
    F -->|"remember"| H["Note kept for the named stages"]
    F -->|"discard"| I["Nothing reaches an agent"]
```

### Where a held answer waits

- **Spec and plan gates:** the fold stores the answer in `held_answers` as a `HeldAnswer` (`Questions`, `Approval`, or `Recurring`). It marks the spec or plan track as routing, so no agent starts. The planner then starts `RouteAnswer` with the gate ID.
- **Phase gates:** a `review_cap`, `stuck`, or `phase_blocked` answer with text sets the loop to `LoopNext::AwaitRoute`. If the judge delivers nothing, the loop uses its fallback: `stuck` blocks the phase, `review_cap` runs the plain fix pass, and `phase_blocked` runs the plain fix pass.
- **Implementation review:** `feedback` creates a feedback round. The planner starts `Feedback` with the round index. The judge picks the route and one target for each project that must change.
- **Context added to a running session:** `RequestAmended` carries `routed: true` after classification. The planner starts `RouteAnswer` with `amendment:N` and starts nothing else until the judge decides. A `Now` delivery stopped the running work, and the work re-runs with the context unless the judge discards it.

### What happens when

- **The user approved a version that is no longer current:** the engine does not approve it. The judge still routes the text.
- **The judge delivers a requirement change after the spec exists:** the engine adds the text to the spec changes and runs the spec agent again. The spec needs a new fact-check and a new approval.
- **The session has no spec:** a delivered answer goes to the agent that asked, whatever the route.
- **The judge asks for research:** the engine queues the tasks and gives the agent the new documents with the answer.

## YOLO mode

YOLO mode is a switch of one session. When it is on, the engine answers gates itself and records each answer with the source `yolo` and a reason. Two gate kinds stay open, as [Gates that stay open under YOLO](#gates-that-stay-open-under-yolo) explains. YOLO changes who answers. It never changes what must be true. Guards, deny rules, the fact-check `PASS` before approval, and the removal of `BLOCKER` security findings still apply.

### Turn YOLO on or off

- **New task form:** the `YOLO` switch sets `SessionOptions.yolo`.
- **Workspace setting:** `yolo.default` in the workspace settings sets `yolo` for every new session. The private `start_session` in [`runner.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs) (lines 356-372) applies it. `Engine::create_session` and the init flow call `start_session`. Read [Configuration reference](configuration.md) for the setting.
- **Running session:** `POST /api/sessions/{id}/yolo` with `SetYolo { enabled }` calls `Engine::set_yolo`. It appends `YoloSet`. The session board has a `YOLO` switch for this call.

The fold keeps the flag in `SessionState.yolo`, so the flag survives a server restart. When the user switches YOLO on, `set_yolo` answers each open `permission` gate with `allow-once` at once. It gives the reason `YOLO was switched on, so every permission ask is allowed.` Other open gates get an answer in the next planner pass.

In a YOLO session, the policy turns each `ask` result into an allow result. The result has layer `permission` and rule `yolo`. The code is `RuleRef::permission("yolo")` in [`policy.rs`](crates/ostra-policy/src/policy.rs). Layer 1 guards and deny rules run first, so they still apply.

### The YOLO answer path

The planner pushes `Step::YoloAnswer { gate }` for each open gate in a YOLO session. It skips a `permission` gate, because the live execution answers it. It also skips a gate that `yolo_leaves_open` names.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Open gate in a YOLO session"] --> B{"Permission gate or left open"}
    B -->|"yes"| C["No planner answer"]
    B -->|"no"| D["Planner pushes YoloAnswer"]
    D --> E{"yolo_plan result"}
    E -->|"Fixed"| H["Fixed answer and reason"]
    E -->|"Judge"| F["call_judge with the YoloAnswer schema"]
    F -->|"call fails"| G["Note event and the gate waits"]
    F --> I["yolo_answer_from_judge checks"]
    I -->|"refused"| G
    I -->|"accepted"| H
    H --> J["GateAnswered with source yolo"]
```

`perform_yolo` in `runner.rs` runs the path. `yolo_plan` returns `YoloPlan::Fixed { answer, reason }` or `YoloPlan::Judge { schema }`. A fixed plan needs no model call. A judge plan builds a schema for the `answer` field of the `YoloAnswer` judge. The runner then sets `routed` with `answer_needs_route`, so a YOLO answer with text goes through the `RouteAnswer` judge like a user answer.

### Gates that stay open under YOLO

Under YOLO, `budget_reached` and an `execution_failed` gate for an execution that the user stopped stay open. The function `yolo_leaves_open` in `judge_input.rs` names both: it returns true for every `BudgetReached` payload, and for an `ExecutionFailed` payload when `SessionState::stopped_by_user` is true for its execution.

The reasons differ for each gate:

- **`budget_reached`:** spending more money is the decision of the user.
- **`execution_failed` after a user stop (Rule P4):** the user decides whether to retry work that the user stopped.

An `execution_failed` gate for an execution that failed by itself does not stay open. The table below shows its YOLO answer.

### The YOLO answer for each gate

| Gate | Plan | The YOLO answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open_questions` | Judge | One answer for each question. The schema fixes the count to the number of questions. The engine fills a missing answer with the label of the recommended option. |
| `spec_approval`, `plan_approval` | Judge | `approved` and `feedback`. The engine accepts `approved: true` only after a fact-check `PASS` on the current version. A rejection needs feedback. |
| `stuck` | Judge | `fact` with text, or `block`. The engine turns `fact` without text into `block`. |
| `implementation_review` | Fixed | `done`. The reason says that only the user can say what to change. |
| `closing_gate` | Fixed | For each project, tests and docs only when the request already asked for them. Otherwise no. |
| `fact_check_recurring` | Fixed | `another-round` when `passes` is below 6. Otherwise `stop`. |
| `review_cap` | Fixed | `another-pass`. |
| `phase_blocked` | Fixed | `leave`. Independent work continues (Rule D9). |
| `execution_failed` | Fixed | `retry` when fewer than 2 earlier gates of the same agent got an answer. Otherwise `abandon`. The planner skips the gate if the user stopped the execution. |
| `harness_failure` | Fixed | `native`. |
| `skill_approval` | Fixed | The default dispositions of the proposal. |
| `permission` | Fixed | `allow-once`. The host records it when the execution asks. |
| `budget_reached` | none | The gate stays open. Spending more is the decision of the user. |

In a YOLO session the policy changes each `ask` result to an allow result with layer `permission` and rule `yolo` (`RuleRef::permission("yolo")` in [`policy.rs`](crates/ostra-policy/src/policy.rs), line 388). Layer 1 guards run first, and deny rules stay in force. Read [Policy engine](policy.md) for these rules. When an ask still reaches the host, `ask_permission` in [`runner.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs) (line 2896, branch `if st.yolo`) opens the `permission` gate. It then answers the gate with `allow-once` and the reason `Under YOLO every permission ask is allowed.` The event source is `yolo`.

### What YOLO keeps

- **The fact-check:** `yolo_answer_from_judge` returns the error `approval requires a fact-check PASS` for an approval without a pass. A rejection without feedback returns `a rejection needs feedback saying what to change`.
- **The gate list:** a gate kind that has a fixed plan returns the error `this gate is answered without the judge` when the judge path receives it.
- **The budget:** the `budget_reached` gate stays open.
- **The fact-check cap:** YOLO runs 3 more rounds, then stops the session at 6 failed passes.
- **Security findings:** a `BLOCKER` finding loops with no cap until the review passes. No judge sees it.

### What happens when

- **The YOLO judge call fails 3 times:** the runner appends a `Note` event with the text `YOLO could not answer "<title>": <error>. The gate waits for you.` The gate stays open. Because YOLO is still on, a later planner pass can start the step again.
- **The engine refuses the judge answer:** the runner appends the note `The YOLO answer was refused: <reason>. The gate waits for you.`
- **The user answers first:** `perform_yolo` checks that the gate has no answer before it appends. The fold also ignores a second answer.
- **The user switches YOLO off:** the planner stops pushing YOLO steps. Open gates wait for the user. Answered gates stay answered.
- **The session is paused:** the planner starts no YOLO answer.
- **A gate opens in a YOLO session:** the console sends no push notice. The exception is `harness_failure`, because the user must log in.

The completion judge receives the gates that YOLO answered. Its report has a `Decided for you` section with one line for each decision. The user can read each reason there and on the gate card.

## The review loop under YOLO

A review loop runs fix passes and review passes until no HIGH or MEDIUM finding stays open. [Sessions and the pipeline](sessions-and-pipeline.md) owns the loop caps: `REVIEW_CAP`, `YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET`, `FACTCHECK_RECURRING_LIMIT`, and `extra_cap`. This part covers only what happens when a loop reaches its cap.

The behavior at the cap depends on YOLO:

- **YOLO is off:** the loop opens a `review_cap` gate. The user picks another pass or stops.
- **YOLO is on:** the loop calls the `ResolveReview` judge. The judge reads the ledger and the open findings.

The judge answers `fix` or `block`:

- **`fix`:** the engine runs one fix pass with one instruction for each finding, then one verification review. It raises `resolve_rounds` by 1 and `extra_cap` by 1. If `instructions` is empty, the engine uses the plain fix instructions.
- **`block`:** the engine blocks the phase with the text `The engine could not resolve the open review findings: <reason>. Ledger: <path>`.

After the verification review, findings can remain. The loop then calls the judge again only if the open count fell below the count before the last resolution. Otherwise it blocks the phase. The text says that the loop stopped converging after N resolution rounds.

A blocked phase in a YOLO session opens no `phase_blocked` gate. The engine announces the block and records the open findings and the ledger path. It removes the phases that depend on the blocked phase. Independent phases continue (Rule D9).

If the user switches YOLO on while a loop waits at its cap, the loop calls `ResolveReview` at the next planner pass. An already open `review_cap` gate gets the YOLO answer `another-pass`.

## Autofix of review findings

Many review findings are exact one-line edits, such as a rename or a comment. A fix agent run for each of them costs a full execution. Autofix applies such an edit as a text change in [`autofix.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/autofix.rs), with no model call.

### Which findings qualify

1. The project profile `.ostra/project.toml` lists review rules. A rule with `auto_fixable` set can qualify. `ProjectProfile::auto_fixable_ids` returns the rule IDs and drops `SEC-BLOCK*` and `PHASE-REQ*`.
2. When the runner spawns a review execution, it stores these IDs in the execution params under `auto_fixable_ids` (`AUTO_FIXABLE_PARAM`). The fold reads them from the log, so the fold stays a pure function of the log.
3. After the review, a finding is auto-fixable if its severity is not `BLOCKER`, its rule does not start with `SEC-BLOCK` or `PHASE-REQ`, and its rule ID is in the stored list.
4. A `BLOCKER` finding or a security block goes alone to the fix agent before any of this. That path has no cap (Hard rule 21).

The fold sorts the findings of a review into three groups:

- **Apply:** the auto-fixable findings.
- **Remaining:** HIGH and MEDIUM findings that are not auto-fixable.
- **Left over:** LOW findings that are not auto-fixable. They stay open and appear in the completion report.

### How the engine applies them

If the apply group is not empty, the loop state becomes `LoopNext::Autofix { apply, remaining }`. The planner pushes `Step::Autofix`. The runner calls `autofix::apply_findings` on a blocking thread and appends `AutofixApplied { project, phase, tests, applied, failed }`.

The reviewer writes the `fix` text of an auto-fixable finding in one of two exact forms. The prefix `Fix:` is optional. Double backticks around a span let it hold a backtick.

- ``Change `old` to `new` on line N.``
- ``Add `text` above line N: `anchor`.``

`parse_fix` returns `Fix::Replace { old, new, line }` or `Fix::Add { text, line, anchor }`. It returns `None` for any other text. `apply_findings` then works in this order:

1. Group the fixes by file and sort each group by line, highest first. A fix near the end of a file then does not shift the lines of the earlier fixes.
2. Reject a path that `is_inside` does not accept as inside the project root.
3. Read the file. Apply each fix with `apply_fix`.
4. Write the file once, when at least one fix applied.

`apply_fix` follows these rules. Lines count from 1.

- The old text or the anchor must be on the named line, or within 2 lines of it. The search order is the line, the line before, the line after, then 2 lines before and 2 lines after. Earlier fixes in the same file can shift lines.
- A replacement needs a non-empty old text that appears exactly once on the line that the search finds.
- An addition inserts the text above the anchor line. It copies the indent of the anchor line, unless the text starts with white space.
- The function keeps a final newline when the file had one.

### What the fold does with the result

The fold reads `failed` from `AutofixApplied`. A failed HIGH or MEDIUM finding returns to the remaining group. It then calls `after_findings` with the remaining findings:

- **Nothing remains:** the loop goes to the stage command (`git add`) or to done. The engine starts no new review pass for the applied edits.
- **Findings remain and the cap is not reached:** the loop runs a fix pass with the findings that remain.
- **Findings remain and the cap is reached:** the loop opens a `review_cap` gate, or calls `ResolveReview` in a YOLO session.

### Why a finding fails

`failed` holds pairs of the finding text (`ReviewFinding::line()`) and a reason:

- `the Fix text is not in an auto-fixable form`
- `the file is outside the project`
- `<file> could not be read`
- `` `old` is not on or near line N ``
- `` `old` appears more than once on line N ``
- `the old text is empty`
- `the anchor is not on or near line N`
- `write failed: <error>`, with the file name in the first position

Autofix is not an agent tool call, so the policy engine does not see it. The check `is_inside` is the only path check. Write the rule IDs in `auto_fixable` only for exact mechanical edits, because no review pass checks the edit when nothing else remains.

## The judge prompts in assets/judges

The folder `assets/judges` holds one Markdown file for each judge. `ostra_agents::judge_prompt(name)` returns the text. The crate embeds the files in the binary with `RustEmbed`. The test `judges_and_references_resolve` in `ostra-agents` checks that all ten prompts exist and that each prompt names the `decide` tool. [Agents, prompts, and the spawn contract](agents-and-prompts.md) owns the rest of `assets`.

### The parts of a prompt

Every prompt has a purpose paragraph, an `Input` part that lists what the user message holds, and an `Output` part that ends with the call `decide`. The middle part has a different name in some files:

- **Eight prompts have a `Decide` part with the rules:** `classify.md`, `sufficiency.md`, `track.md`, `stakes.md`, `feedback.md`, `rescue.md`, `resolve-review.md`, and `route-answer.md`.
- **`completion.md`** has a `Write` part in place of `Decide`.
- **`yolo-answer.md`** names the part `Decide, by gate kind`.
- **`route-answer.md`** also adds a `The user decides` part before `Decide`, and a `Context the user added` part after it.

The prompts tell the judge what to do when it doubts:

| Prompt | The rules that the judge follows |
| --- | --- |
| `classify.md` | Pick the category by what the request asks Ostra to produce. If two categories fit, pick the one with more pipeline. If none fits, pick `RESEARCH`. `QUICK_CHANGE` is only for an edit that needs nothing beyond its own lines. An edit of a prompt, a `SKILL.md`, or an agent file is `PROMPT`. A pin limits the projects to the pinned keys. The title has 2 to 5 words. |
| `sufficiency.md` | A `Not covered` item is needed when the request depends on it. If the judge cannot tell, it marks the item needed. |
| `stakes.md` | Any doubt resolves upward, because skipping the plan removes the phase review. |
| `track.md` | `light` is the default. `full` needs evidence: an open behavior, a changed contract, a schema or data change, ordered work across modules, security, or a new codebase. |
| `route-answer.md` | The words of the user win over the recommendation. `deliver` is the default. `discard` needs the words of the user. `remember` needs an answer that is wholly for a later stage. Doubt resolves to `requirement_change`. With no spec, pick `implementation_detail`. |
| `feedback.md` | `requirement_change` only when a requirement addresses the subject. With no spec, always `implementation_detail`. Targets are only the projects whose files change. |
| `rescue.md` | `rerun` needs a known fact. `explore` needs a fact that the code or documents hold. `gate` needs a fact that only the user has. After 2 rescues with the same diagnostic, choose `gate`. The engine does not enforce this rule. |
| `resolve-review.md` | `fix` needs an exact instruction that breaks the cycle. `block` fits findings that do not converge or need a fact only the user has. |
| `yolo-answer.md` | Decide by gate kind. Never invent a requirement, a rule, or a fact. When a gate needs a fact that only the user has, choose the answer that sets the work aside. |
| `completion.md` | Write `Summary`, `Phases`, `Checks`, `Not run`, `Blocked`, and, under YOLO, `Decided for you`. State facts and report every stage that did not run. |

### Which gate kinds the YOLO prompt names

The `Decide, by gate kind` part of `yolo-answer.md` lists these kinds: open questions, spec or plan approval, closing gate, review cap, stuck, permission, harness failure, and skill approval. It does not list `phase_blocked`.

The engine does not send every listed kind to the judge. `yolo_plan` answers five of the listed kinds with a fixed plan and no prompt: `closing_gate`, `review_cap`, `permission`, `harness_failure`, and `skill_approval`. The judge answers only `open_questions`, `spec_approval`, `plan_approval`, and `stuck`. The engine also answers `implementation_review`, `fact_check_recurring`, `phase_blocked`, and `execution_failed` with a fixed plan, and the prompt does not list them. The code is the source of truth, and the table in [The YOLO answer for each gate](#the-yolo-answer-for-each-gate) shows the real answers.

A change to a judge prompt changes model behavior that no unit test checks. Run the judge evals after you edit a file in `assets/judges`.

## The gate cards in the console

The folder `web/src/features/gates` holds one card for each gate kind. `GateCard` shows the answer form while the gate is open and the recorded answer after the answer. The anchor `#gate-<id>` links to the card.

| Gate kind | Component | Controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open_questions` | `QuestionsGate` | One fieldset for each question, an `Other` field, and the button `Send the answers`. |
| `spec_approval`, `plan_approval` | `ApprovalGate` | The chip `Fact-check PASS`, the LOW findings, a text field, and the buttons `Approve the spec` or `Approve the plan` and `Request changes to ...`. The approve button stays off while the text field has text. The plan card also shows a table of the phases. |
| The 8 choice gates | `ChoiceGate` | One button for each entry in `CHOICES`, and a text field when the gate takes text. |
| `closing_gate` | `ClosingGate` | One group for each project. A checkbox appears only for a question that the request did not already decide. |
| `permission` | `PermissionGate` | `Allow once`, `Always in this workspace` (off when the call has no suggested rule), and `Deny`. |
| `skill_approval` | `SkillsGate` | A table with a select for each skill: generate, regenerate, reuse, or drop. |

`CHOICES` in `gateAnswers.ts` lists the buttons of the choice gates. One option in each gate is primary.

| Gate | Buttons, with the option in parentheses |
| --- | --- |
| `fact_check_recurring` | `Run another fact-check round` (`another-round`), `Stop the session` (`stop`) |
| `review_cap` | `Run another fix and review pass` (`another-pass`), `Stop and block the phase` (`stop`) |
| `stuck` | `Re-run with this fact` (`fact`, text required), `Block this work` (`block`) |
| `phase_blocked` | `Retry the phase` (`retry`), `Leave the phase blocked` (`leave`) |
| `harness_failure` | `Retry after login` (`retry`), `Run on the native executor` (`native`) |
| `execution_failed` | `Retry the execution` (`retry`), `Abandon this work` (`abandon`) |
| `budget_reached` | `Raise the budget` (`raise`), `Stop the session` (`stop`) |
| `implementation_review` | `Accept the implementation` (`done`), `Send feedback` (`feedback`, text required) |

The budget field accepts a positive number, with or without a leading `$`. The engine parses the same form. An empty field, or a value that is not a positive number, adds the current budget again. The console shows an error for a value that is not a number: `Enter the amount as a number of US dollars, such as 10. Leave it empty to add the budget again.`

An answered card shows one line from `answerSummary`. It also shows who answered. A `yolo` answer shows the YOLO label and the reason of the judge. An `engine` answer starts with `Closed by Ostra:`.

`BlockerNotice` is not a gate. It shows a `security_block` event as a banner. The banner has no dismiss button, because only a passing review clears a `BLOCKER` finding (Hard rule 21).

## Judge evals

The test `judge_routing_evals` in [`judge_evals.rs`](crates/ostra-server/tests/judge_evals.rs) calls the real judge models. It reads the cases from `tests/evals/judges.toml`. The file holds 83 cases for 6 judges: `classify`, `feedback`, `route_answer`, `stakes`, `sufficiency`, and `track`. Each case builds the session state with the same fold and the same `judge_input` as the engine. The test ignores itself by default, because it costs money.

```text
OSTRA_EVAL_MODELS=anthropic:claude-opus-5-5 OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS=3 \
  cargo test -p ostra-server --test judge_evals -- --ignored --nocapture
```

- `OSTRA_EVAL_MODELS` lists models, separated by commas. The default is `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5`.
- `OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS` sets the calls for each model and case. The default is 3.
- `OSTRA_EVAL_CASES` keeps the cases whose ID contains one of the listed texts.
- The test writes a report to `target/evals/judges-<time>.json`. It fails only when every call fails.

The offline test `eval_cases_build_their_sessions` runs with `cargo test --workspace`. It checks that each case folds into the state that its judge expects. [Tests and evals](testing.md) explains all test layers.
