sections.title: Code navigation
sections.summary: How the ostra-code crate and the server turn project files into colors, outlines, usages, dependencies, and a graph, and how language servers and custom programs replace the built-in answer.
sections.body:
Code navigation gives the Files view colors, an outline, usages, and dependencies for a source file. It gives agents the same facts as text. Without it, a reader sees plain text and an agent finds a symbol only with text search. A language server answers well, but it needs a project build, and many projects have none. The `ostra-code` crate answers for 16 languages with no build and no outside program. A project can add language servers or its own program for better answers.

This page covers:

- the language table, the lexer, outlines, and import resolution
- the incremental index, usages, and the dependency graph
- the eight code tools for agents
- the provider chain, custom `code_provider` programs, and language servers
- editor hints and the file watcher
- the routes, the limits, and the cases that change an answer

## Where the code lives

The `ostra-code` crate has no server code. The server crate builds the provider chain for each request and feeds file changes to the index.

| Path | Job |
| --- | --- |
| [`crates/ostra-core/src/code.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/code.rs) | The contracts: `CodeFile`, `CodeUsages`, `CodeDeps`, `CodeSymbols`, `CodeGraph`, `ProviderRequest`, `PROTOCOL_VERSION`, and `NAV_LANGUAGES`. |
| [`crates/ostra-code/src/lang.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/lang.rs) | The language table. |
| [`crates/ostra-code/src/lex.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/lex.rs) | The tokenizer. |
| [`crates/ostra-code/src/outline.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/outline.rs) | Display classes, definitions, supertype links, and raw imports. |
| [`crates/ostra-code/src/resolve.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/resolve.rs) | Import resolution to project files. |
| [`crates/ostra-code/src/index.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/index.rs) | `ProjectIndex` and `Indexes`: the incremental index. |
| [`crates/ostra-code/src/usage.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/usage.rs) | Usages by meaning (`usages_at`). |
| [`crates/ostra-code/src/graph.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/graph.rs) | The dependency graph, callers, callees, impact, and graph views. |
| [`crates/ostra-code/src/provider.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/provider.rs) | The `CodeProvider` trait, `ask`, `NativeProvider`, and `CommandProvider`. |
| [`crates/ostra-code/src/lsp/mod.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/lsp/mod.rs) | `LspPool` and `LspProvider`. The folder also holds `rpc.rs`, `convert.rs`, and `external.rs`. |
| [`crates/ostra-code/src/hint.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/hint.rs) | Editor completions and jumps that the index answers. |
| [`crates/ostra-code/src/tools.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/tools.rs) | The text answers of the agent code tools. |
| [`crates/ostra-server/src/code.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/code.rs) | `Code` (the chain builder) and `CodeTools` (the agent bridge). |
| [`crates/ostra-server/src/code_watch.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/code_watch.rs) | The file watcher. |
| [`assets/code-tools.md`](assets/code-tools.md) | The guide text that agents with code tools read. |

The routes that expose code navigation are in [Server, REST API, and WebSocket](server-and-api.md). The settings that name providers are in [Configuration reference](configuration.md).

## The language table and the lexer

The language table is the one place that describes a language. `lang::ALL` holds 22 `Lang` entries. Each entry has an `id`, a `Family`, comment and string syntax, keywords, built-in types, constants, and the keywords that start a definition (`defs`). One entry serves display, outline, usages, and imports.

`lang::for_path` picks the language from the extension, compared in lower case, or from a few file names. `Makefile` and `Dockerfile` have no language.

| Language id | Extensions and names |
| --- | --- |
| `rust` | `rs` |
| `typescript` | `ts`, `tsx`, `mts`, `cts` |
| `javascript` | `js`, `jsx`, `mjs`, `cjs` |
| `python` | `py`, `pyi` |
| `go` | `go` |
| `java` | `java` |
| `kotlin` | `kt`, `kts` |
| `scala` | `scala`, `sc` |
| `csharp` | `cs` |
| `swift` | `swift` |
| `php` | `php` |
| `c` | `c`, `h` |
| `cpp` | `cc`, `cpp`, `cxx`, `hpp`, `hh`, `hxx`, `ipp`, `m`, `mm` |
| `ruby` | `rb`, `rake`, `gemspec`, `Gemfile`, `Rakefile` |
| `lua` | `lua` |
| `shell` | `sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, `.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, `.profile` |

These 16 ids are `NAV_LANGUAGES` in `ostra-core`. A `language_servers` entry can name only these ids.

Six more languages are in the table for color only: `sql`, `toml`, `yaml` (`yaml`, `yml`), `json` (`json`, `jsonc`), `css` (`css`, `scss`, `less`), and `html` (`html`, `htm`, `xml`, `svg`, `vue`, `svelte`). They have the family `Data`. `Lang::indexed` returns false for them, so they have no definitions, no imports, and no place in the index.

### Language families

A family groups languages that share definition and import rules.

| Family | Languages |
| --- | --- |
| `Rust` | `rust` |
| `Js` | `typescript`, `javascript` |
| `Python` | `python` |
| `Go` | `go` |
| `Jvm` | `java`, `kotlin`, `scala`, `csharp`, `swift`, `php` |
| `C` | `c`, `cpp` |
| `Ruby`, `Lua`, `Shell` | one language each |
| `Data` | `sql`, `toml`, `yaml`, `json`, `css`, `html` |

### The lexer

`lex::lex` is table-driven and never fails. It skips text that it does not understand. A token holds byte offsets for the analysis, a 1-based line, and a column and length in UTF-16 code units, which match a browser string index. A comment or string that spans lines becomes one token for each line.

`render` in [`crates/ostra-code/src/lib.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/lib.rs) builds the `CodeFile` answer. Each token that has a display class becomes four numbers in the flat `tokens` list: line, column, length, and an index into `classes`. The `classes` list is the constant `CLASSES`, which holds 11 `TokenClass` values: `keyword`, `type`, `function`, `name`, `constant`, `macro`, `attribute`, `string`, `number`, `comment`, and `operator`. Punctuation has no class and has no entry. The browser offers Find usages on the classes for which `TokenClass::is_symbol` is true: `type`, `function`, `name`, `constant`, and `macro`.

## Outlines and imports

One pass over the tokens, `outline::analyze`, produces the display classes, the definitions, the supertype links, and the raw imports. Definitions come from keyword rules (`fn`, `class`, `def`), member rules inside class bodies, and a few family forms: C function bodies, Go receivers, and Python indentation. The pass matches names by text and has no type information. This is the reason that every answer of the index is a name match and not a type match.

A `CodeSymbol` has a `name`, a `kind`, a 1-based `line`, a 0-based UTF-16 `col`, an optional `end_line`, an optional `container`, and an optional `via`. The `kind` is one of `function`, `method`, `class`, `enum`, `interface`, `type`, `module`, `constant`, `variable`, `field`, and `macro`. The `via` field names the trait or interface of the enclosing impl block, such as `Display` for a `fmt` in `impl Display for Point`. A `Super` link records that one type names another as its supertype: `class A extends B`, `impl B for A`, or `trait A: B`.

A raw import has a `spec`, a `line`, and a style. The styles are `Use` (Rust `use`, Python, Java, C#, PHP), `Mod` (Rust `mod name;`), `Module` (a string spec in JS, Go, and Lua), `Include`, and `Require`. A JS import also keeps the names that it brings in, and an `export * from` marks a star import.

## Import resolution

The `Resolver` turns a raw import into a project file or folder. It reads only the project file list and the manifests in it. The result is a `Target` with a project-relative `path` and a `folder` flag. A `null` target means an external package. The folder flag is true for a Go package or a wildcard import.

The resolver reads these manifests: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `go.mod`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts`, `composer.json`, `Gemfile`, `Package.swift`, `mix.exs`, and files that end in `.csproj`, `.gemspec`, or `.rockspec`. A folder that holds a manifest is a package. `unit_of_dir` returns the nearest package folder of a path, or the empty string for the project top.

| Family | How the resolver finds the target |
| --- | --- |
| `Rust` | Follows `crate::`, `self::`, `super::`, and other crate names from `Cargo.toml` names (a `-` becomes `_`). A `mod name;` finds `name.rs` or `name/mod.rs`. |
| `Js` | Handles relative specs, `@/` and `~/` aliases, workspace packages from `package.json` (`exports`, `module`, `main`), and absolute specs. It tries the extensions `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.d.ts`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.vue`, `.svelte`, and `index` files. A `.js` spec also finds a `.ts` or `.tsx` file. |
| `Python` | Handles relative dots and absolute modules. It tries `.py`, `.pyi`, and `__init__.py`, then a folder. |
| `Go` | Matches the `module` line of `go.mod` and returns a folder. |
| `Jvm` | Matches a dotted path as a file suffix with the extensions of the language. It prefers the file that shares the most path segments with the importer. A `.*` import returns a folder. |
| `C` | Tries a quoted include relative to the file, the project top, `include/`, and `src/`. Then it matches a path suffix. |
| `Ruby`, `Lua`, `Shell` | Try `lib/` or the project top, relative paths, and a path suffix. |
| `Data` | No imports. |

The index caches one resolver for each file list. When the file list object changes, the index builds a new resolver. The server passes the same resolver to `NativeProvider` for file answers.

## The incremental index

`ProjectIndex` keeps, for each indexed file, the sorted set of names that the file mentions, its definitions, its imports, and its supertype links. It never keeps the text. A usages query reads again only the files that mention the name. Memory use therefore depends on the number of names, not on the size of the source.

`Indexes<K>` holds one index for each project, keyed by `(workspace id, project key)`. The first call for a project builds the index. Every query goes through `Indexes::with`, which brings the index up to date, then runs the query. `with` blocks, and the first call for a project reads every source file. The server runs it inside `spawn_blocking`.

### How `with` brings the index up to date

1. `with` takes the paths that were touched since the last query, then builds or reuses the resolver for the current file list.
2. If the file list object changed, or more than 30 seconds (`FULL_SYNC`) passed since the last full check, `with` calls `sync` on every listed path. Files that left the list are removed.
3. Otherwise, if some paths were touched, `with` calls `sync` on only those paths.
4. `sync` takes a size and modification time stamp of each path. A file with the same stamp is not analyzed again. `sync` analyzes the other files on up to 8 worker threads (`index::parallel`).
5. The query runs on the updated index.

The touched paths live in a separate lock from the index. A write therefore never waits for a build. Writers call `Indexes::touch`, which only records the path.

### Which files the index skips

The index holds a file only if all of these are true:

- The file is in the project file list. The list leaves out files that `.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude`, and the global git ignore file exclude. The list holds at most 50,000 files (`INDEX_CAP`) and expires after 30 seconds.
- The language is not `Data`.
- The file size is at most 1 MiB (`MAX_FILE_BYTES`).
- The first 8,000 bytes hold no NUL byte.
- The text is not minified. A file counts as minified when it is larger than 50,000 bytes and has more than 1,000 bytes on an average line.
- The index holds less than 256 MiB of source (`MAX_INDEX_BYTES`). When the cap stops a file, `ProjectIndex::truncated` becomes true, and answers carry the warning "The project is larger than the size Ostra indexes, so some files are not searched."

A file that grows over a cap is removed from the index at the next `sync`.

### Reindex

`POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/projects/{key}/code/reindex` drops the cached file list, calls `Indexes::forget`, and builds the index again. It returns `CodeReindex` with `indexed_files`, `millis`, and `truncated`. It does not stop language servers.

## Usages

A usages request has two forms. The server sends the form with a position when the request has `path` and `line`. Otherwise it sends the name-only form.

- **Name only** (`ProjectIndex::usages`): Every definition of the name is a definition, and every other mention is a reference. The query reads only files that mention the name, at most 4,000 of them (`MAX_SCAN_FILES`). It reads the file that the request names first, then files in the same folder, then the rest by path.
- **By meaning** (`usages_at`): The token nearest to the given column picks the target. A position on a definition means that definition. On a use, the index resolves what the use means and keeps only the references that can mean the same definition.

To resolve a use, `usages_at` looks at the declared type of the receiver (`Repo repo`, `repo: Repo`, `repo = new Repo()`), then at the supertypes of that type, up to 8 hops (`MAX_SUPER_DEPTH`). It follows call chains up to 6 calls (`MAX_CHAIN`). It sees through wrapper types such as `Box`, `Arc`, `Option`, `Result`, and `Promise`, and through calls such as `unwrap`, `orElseThrow`, and `clone`. It also adds the interface methods that a target method implements, because a call through the interface can reach the target. This keeps `a.name` and `b.name` of two unrelated classes apart.

When the index cannot tell what a use means, `usages_at` falls back to the name-only form. The answer then lists every definition and use of the name.

The answer is a `CodeUsages` value: `definitions`, `references`, `truncated`, and an optional `warning`. The route default for `limit` is 500 and the cap is 2,000 (`DEFAULT_USAGES`, `MAX_USAGES`). When the result reaches the limit, `truncated` is true.

### Dependencies and symbol search

`ProjectIndex::deps` returns what a file imports, each with its resolved target, and which files import it. For a Go package, it also returns the files that import the folder. It lists at most 2,000 importers (`MAX_IMPORTERS`).

`ProjectIndex::symbols` finds definitions by name. It scores each name: 110 for an exact match, 100 for a match that ignores case, 80 for a prefix, 60 for a substring, and 40 for initials. For example, `pn` finds `parse_name` and `ParseName`. Initials need at least 2 letters. Ties go to the shorter name, then to the alphabetical order. The route default for `limit` is 50 and the cap is 200 (`DEFAULT_SYMBOLS`, `MAX_SYMBOLS`).

## The dependency graph

The graph comes from the index. It reads no file when it builds. The index builds it on the first graph query after a link and drops it at the next link. Each file has outgoing and incoming edges.

An edge has two parts. An import edge comes from the resolver. A reference edge links a file to the files that define the names that it mentions.

### How a mention finds its definition

For each mention, `resolve` searches the way a reader looks. It ranks a candidate file by `tier`:

| Tier | Candidate file |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The file that the mentioning file imports, or a file in an imported folder |
| 1 | A file in the same folder |
| 2 | A file in the same package |
| 3 | A file in a package that the mentioning package imports |

A definition in the mentioning file wins first. Otherwise only the nearest tier counts. Several rules reduce wrong links:

- A name that is defined in more than 3 files (`MAX_DEF_FILES`) links none of them, unless the mentioning file imports the defining file directly.
- A file sees another file only within a maximum tier. The maximum is 0 for `Js` and `Python`, 1 for `Go`, and 3 for the other families. A re-export or an import that spells the name can extend it.
- A name of one character links nothing.
- A mention links only to files of the same family. A test file is a candidate only for a mentioning test file.
- Across packages, a bare name links only to a type, a macro, or a top-level constant. A function of another package must come qualified or imported by name.
- A qualified mention (`Thing::go`, `server.Start`) matches the container or the module name first. A member of an unknown receiver matches only a member of a type that the file names.

A path is a test file when it is in a folder named `test`, `tests`, `__tests__`, `spec`, `specs`, `testdata`, or `fixtures`, or when its name matches a test pattern such as `_test.go`, `.test.`, `.spec.`, or `test_`. A file is a hub when its name is `lib`, `main`, `mod`, `index`, or `__init__`, or when it has an `export * from`. A walk does not follow an edge that only declares a Rust `mod`, because that edge shows containment and not use. A walk also does not follow an import-only edge into a hub, because the names already link to the defining files.

### Graph queries

| Query | What it returns |
| --- | --- |
| `neighbors` | The files that one file uses and the files that use it, with import lines and up to 8 shared names for each link. |
| `reach` | A walk by hops in one direction. It stops at 5,000 files (`MAX_REACH`). |
| `related` | Direct links by strength, then files one step further that share them. A file with more than 200 links is not a stepping stone (`MAX_BRIDGE_DEGREE`). |
| `hubs` | The files that the most other files depend on. |
| `units` and `cycles` | The packages with their link counts, and loops of packages or files. |
| `callers` | The definitions that mention a symbol, with lines. It reads at most 5,000 references (`MAX_CALLER_REFS`). |
| `callees` | The definitions that the body of one definition names, in order of first mention. |
| `symbol_impact` | The definitions that use a symbol, then those that use them, hop by hop. |
| `implementations` | What a type or method implements and what implements it. |

### Graph views for the Files view

`GET .../code/graph` returns a `CodeGraph` with a `view`: `packages`, `package`, `file`, or `symbol`. Pass no `path` and no `package` for `packages`. Pass `package` (use `.` for the project top) for `package`. Pass `path` for `file`. Pass `path` and `symbol` (and optionally `line`) for `symbol`. Passing both `package` and `path` is an error. The `depth` value is cut to 1 to 3 (`MAX_GRAPH_DEPTH`).

Each node has a `column`. A node sits to the left of the nodes that it uses. Nodes that use each other in a loop share a column. The focus of a file view is column 0. The code finds loops with strongly connected components.

| View cap | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Files in a package view (`MAX_VIEW_FILES`) | 150 |
| Files in a file view (`MAX_VIEW_NEIGHBORS`) | 80 |
| Edges in a symbol view (`MAX_VIEW_EDGES`) | 300 |
| Callees that a symbol view reads for one definition (`MAX_VIEW_CALLEES`) | 200 |
| Members that a type node lists (`MAX_MEMBERS`) | 40 |
| Top-level definitions that a node lists (`MAX_FILE_DEFS`) | 30 |

When a cap cuts a view, `truncated` is true. A symbol view keeps implementation edges first, then the heaviest reference edges. It follows only functions, methods, macros, and types, because edges for fields, variables, and constants hide the calls. The graph always comes from the built-in index. A language server or a custom program does not change it. When the path, package, or symbol is not in the index, the route returns status 404.

## Code tools for agents

Agents that have the `Code` capability call eight tools. The MCP name of each tool is `code_` plus the operation, from `CODE_TOOLS` in [`crates/ostra-core/src/agent.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/agent.rs). [Native tools](tools.md) describes how the tool layer runs them. [Agents, prompts, and the spawn contract](agents-and-prompts.md) describes how the prompt gets the guide.

`render_prompt_in` puts the text of [`assets/code-tools.md`](assets/code-tools.md) before the prompt of each agent that has the `Code` capability. The file is a template. Placeholders such as `{{tool_code_map}}` become the tool names of the executor. The guide tells the agent to call these tools before text search. It also states the limit of the index: the index matches names, not types. An answer can list a definition that only shares the name, or miss a use through a value of a type that the index cannot see. The agent must confirm an answer with text search before it changes code because of the answer.

| Tool | Input | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CodeOutline` | `path`, `limit` | Imports with their targets, then symbols with line ranges, kind, and container. The tool reads the file again from disk. |
| `CodeFind` | `query`, `limit` | Definitions that match the name, ranked as `ProjectIndex::symbols` ranks them. |
| `CodeCallers` | `symbol`, `path`, `limit` | The definitions, then the definitions that mention the symbol, with lines. |
| `CodeCallees` | `path`, `symbol`, `line`, `limit` | The definitions that the body of the symbol names. |
| `CodeImplementations` | `symbol`, `path`, `line`, `limit` | The "implements or extends" and "implemented or extended by" lists. |
| `CodeNeighbors` | `path`, `limit` | Files that the file uses, files that use it, and up to 5 related files through a shared neighbor. |
| `CodeImpact` | `symbol` or `paths`, `path`, `direction`, `depth`, `limit` | The hops of files or definitions that a change can reach, and the files to change or recheck. |
| `CodeMap` | `prefix` | The packages with file and test counts and dependencies, package cycles, the 15 most depended-on files, and up to 10 import cycles. |

The tools have these rules:

- `limit` defaults to 40 and is cut to 1 to 300. `CodeOutline` defaults to 300. `CodeImpact` defaults to 100 and has `depth` 3 by default, cut to 1 to 10.
- A tool rejects an input field that it does not know, with the message "Invalid input".
- `CodeCallers` sets `path` by itself when exactly one file defines the symbol. With several defining files, the answer asks for `path`.
- `CodeImpact` needs exactly one of `symbol` and `paths`. With `symbol`, the walk follows the users of the symbol, so `direction` must not be `dependencies`.
- A path can be project-relative, absolute inside the project, or start with the project folder name. A path that the index does not hold gets an error that names the three causes: an ignored file, a file over 1 MB, or a language that the index does not parse.

`CodeTools` in [`crates/ostra-server/src/code.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/code.rs) implements the `CodeNav` trait of `ostra-tools`. The executors exist before the app, so `CodeTools::bind` attaches the app later. A call finds the innermost project whose folder holds the working directory of the agent. If no project holds it, the call returns an error that says the folder has no code index. A call runs in the server process, on the blocking pool, and it starts the file watcher for the project.

## The provider chain

The Files view asks a chain of providers and takes the first answer. A provider is a `CodeProvider`: it has a `name` and an `answer` method that returns `Ok(Some(answer))`, `Ok(None)`, or `Err(message)`. `Ok(None)` hands the request to the next provider.

`Code::ask` builds the chain for each request. It reads the settings at that time, so a saved change applies to the next request. The order is fixed:

1. The project `code_provider` program, if the settings name one.
2. Each entry of `language_servers`, in the order of the settings.
3. The built-in provider (`NativeProvider`), which is always last.

While the workspace file waits for approval, the settings that the chain reads have no `code_provider` and no `language_servers`. The chain then holds only the built-in provider. See [What happens when a program fails](#what-happens-when-a-program-fails).

The request is one of four kinds: `file`, `usages`, `deps`, or `symbols`. The server checks every path with `files::contain`, so a path must be a file inside the project root.

### The path of a request

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["Request: file, usages, deps, or symbols"] --> C{"code_provider set?"}
  C -->|yes| P["Run the program"]
  C -->|no| L
  P -->|answer| A["Stamp provider name and warnings"]
  P -->|null or error| L{"Next language server entry"}
  L -->|answer| A
  L -->|none or error| N["Built-in index"]
  N --> A
  A --> O["Return the answer"]
```

`provider::ask` loops over the chain. It stamps the answer with the `name` of the provider that answered. If an earlier provider failed, it adds the failure text to the `warning` of the answer. The failure text reads "The code provider `x` failed, so the built-in index answered" and then the reason. The browser shows the provider name and the warning.

If no provider answers and none failed, the error is "No code provider answered this request." The route returns status 400 for a chain error.

### What each provider does for each request

| Request | `code_provider` program | Language server | Built-in provider |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | Returns the whole `CodeFile`. | Starts from the built-in answer. It replaces colors with semantic tokens and the outline with document symbols. Imports stay from the built-in answer. | Tokens, outline, and imports. |
| `usages` | Returns `CodeUsages`. | Definitions and references from the server. | Name-only or by-meaning usages. |
| `deps` | Returns `CodeDeps`. | Always passes (`Ok(None)`). | Imports and importers. |
| `symbols` | Returns `CodeSymbols`. | `workspace/symbol`. | Name scoring. |

The chain does not serve these: graph views, agent code tools, and the index fallback for completions and jumps. They use the built-in index directly.

A built-in `file` answer for a file over 1 MiB has no tokens and no outline. It has the warning "The file is larger than the size Ostra tokenizes, so it shows without color." A language server does not replace such an answer, because the server receives the same cut.

## Custom code_provider programs

A project can name one program that answers navigation requests in place of the built-in index. Ostra runs the program once for each request, in the project folder.

```toml
[projects.code_provider]
command = ["ctags-nav", "--json"]
timeout_secs = 10
```

The `command` list holds the program and its arguments. Its first item must not be empty. `timeout_secs` defaults to 10 and must be from 1 to 120 (`MAX_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT`). The validation rules are in [Configuration reference](configuration.md).

### The protocol

Ostra writes one JSON object and a newline on the standard input of the program. It sets the environment variable `OSTRA_CODE_PROTOCOL` to the protocol version, which is `1` (`PROTOCOL_VERSION`). The object has an `op` field and a `version` field. The `root` field holds the absolute project folder.

| `op` | Other fields | Expected answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | `path` | `CodeFile` |
| `usages` | `symbol`, `path`, `line`, `col`, `limit` | `CodeUsages` |
| `deps` | `path` | `CodeDeps` |
| `symbols` | `query`, `limit` | `CodeSymbols` |

For `usages`, the fields `path`, `line`, and `col` are present only when the user asked from a place in a file. The program writes one JSON value on the standard output. It can write `null` or nothing to leave the request to the next provider. The program can also answer before it reads its input.

This request asks for the usages of a symbol:

```json
{"op":"usages","version":1,"root":"/work/app","symbol":"parse_config","path":"src/main.rs","line":10,"col":4,"limit":500}
```

This answer to a `file` request colors `fn main`:

```json
{"language":"rust","classes":["keyword","name"],"tokens":[1,0,2,0,1,3,4,1],"symbols":[],"imports":[]}
```

The shapes are in [`crates/ostra-core/src/code.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/code.rs). Lines are 1-based. Columns and lengths are 0-based UTF-16 units.

### How Ostra checks the answer

`parse_answer` checks the output before the browser sees it. A failed check makes the answer an error, and the chain goes on to the next provider with a warning.

- The output must be UTF-8 and at most 64 MiB. The text of the program on standard error is kept up to 1 MiB, and the last line goes into the error.
- The answer must match the shape of the request. The error says "Its answer to `op` does not match the protocol".
- `tokens` must hold groups of four numbers, at most 16,777,216 numbers in total. Every token needs a line of 1 or more and a class index inside `classes`.
- Symbols, imports, importers, and locations are limited to 20,000 items each.
- Every path must be project-relative, with no `..`, no `.` segment, no backslash, and no leading slash. Every line must be 1 or more.
- Ostra sets `path` and `symbol` from the request. It fills an empty `name` with the symbol. It clears every `uri`, because Ostra reads back only outside files that a language server named.

### What happens when a program fails

- The program does not start: the error is "Cannot start `program`".
- The program runs longer than `timeout_secs`: Ostra stops it and reports "It took longer than N seconds." The process is killed when its handle is dropped.
- The program exits with a non-zero status: the error holds the status and the last line of its error output.
- The program is not approved: while the workspace file waits for approval, `effective` in [`crates/ostra-workspace/src/trust.rs`](crates/ostra-workspace/src/trust.rs) clears `code_provider` and `language_servers` for every project. The chain then holds only the built-in provider, and language servers do not answer. The same function also disables MCP servers and clears allow rules. See [Workspaces, projects, and approvals](workspaces-and-trust.md).

The program runs through `ostra_sandbox::host_command` under the sandbox settings of the workspace. [Sandbox and egress proxy](sandbox.md) states what that boundary holds and what it does not hold.

## Language servers

A project can name language servers. Each `language_servers` entry has a `command`, a list of `languages`, a `timeout_secs`, and optional `initialization_options`.

```toml
[[projects.language_servers]]
command = ["rust-analyzer"]
languages = ["rust"]
```

The settings reject an empty command, an empty `languages` list, an id that is not in `NAV_LANGUAGES`, and a language in two entries ("each file asks one server"). `timeout_secs` defaults to 10 and must be from 1 to 120. Ostra approves these commands the same way as `code_provider`. An unapproved workspace file disables them, as the section on custom programs states.

### The pool

`LspPool` keeps the running servers. Its key is the project and the command. It follows these rules:

- It starts a server on the first request for one of its languages. `get` starts the server in a separate task, so a caller that stops waiting leaves the server starting for the next caller.
- A request waits at most `timeout_secs` for a server to start. A hint waits at most 3 seconds.
- It stops a server after 10 minutes without a request (`IDLE`). A sweep runs every 60 seconds (`SWEEP`). The sweep removes idle entries and stale entries.
- It keeps at most 8 servers across all projects (`MAX_SERVERS`). Starting one more stops the least recently used server.
- It replaces a server that started under other sandbox settings, so a saved change applies at the next request.

The restart rule uses `Entry::stale`. Each entry records `begun`, the time that the pool created the entry. An entry is stale when its server failed to start, or when its server died, and `begun.elapsed()` is at least 30 seconds (`RETRY`). The delay counts from the start of the entry and not from the failure. A stale entry is replaced at the next request, and the sweep also removes it.

- A server that fails or dies within 30 seconds of its start: the pool does not start it again until 30 seconds pass from `begun`. During that time, the request falls through to the next provider with the failure as a warning.
- A server that ran for more than 30 seconds and then died: the pool starts it again at the next request, with no wait.

`start` runs the command in the project folder under the workspace sandbox, because the server runs the build scripts and macros of the project. It sends `initialize` with a timeout of 60 seconds (`INIT_TIMEOUT`), because some servers read the whole project first. Ostra needs positions in UTF-16. If the server reports another position encoding, Ostra closes it and reports "Ostra needs a server that counts them in utf-16." For a server that lists `java`, Ostra adds `classFileContentsSupport: true` to the initialization options when the user does not set it.

After `initialize`, `Server` keeps at most 32 open documents (`MAX_OPEN`). It sends `didOpen` on the first use of a file and `didChange` when the text hash changes. When it opens a 33rd file, it sends `didClose` for the least recently used one. `LspPool::touch` sends `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles` to the running servers of a project when a file changes or is deleted.

The RPC layer is `rpc::Client`. It uses `Content-Length` framing, accepts messages up to 256 MiB, and keeps the last 20 lines of the server error output. It answers a few server requests (`workspace/configuration`, `workspace/workspaceFolders`, and progress and registration requests) and refuses the others with the code -32601. A request that times out or whose caller stops waiting sends `$/cancelRequest`. A server that reports progress or `quiescent: false` is busy, and answers then carry the warning that the server is still loading the project.

### What a server answers

- **`file`:** The provider takes the built-in answer, then asks for `textDocument/semanticTokens/full` and `textDocument/documentSymbol` in parallel. `convert::overlay` puts the semantic tokens over the built-in tokens. The document symbols replace the outline if the list is not empty. If a call fails, the provider keeps the built-in part and adds a warning. If the server has neither capability and no call failed, the provider passes the request on.
- **`usages`:** With a position, the provider asks `textDocument/definition`, then `textDocument/references` with `includeDeclaration: false`. Without a position, it asks `workspace/symbol` for definitions with the exact name (at most 50), then asks for references from the first one. It leaves out references outside the project, because the uses inside a library hide the uses in the project. It lists the file of the request first, then sorts by path and position. If it finds nothing, it passes the request on.
- **`symbols`:** The provider asks `workspace/symbol`.
- **`deps`:** The provider passes the request on.

A request for a file whose language is not in the `languages` list of the entry passes to the next provider.

### Files outside the project

A server can point at a place outside the project, such as a library source file or a class in a jar. The provider returns such a location with a `uri`. Ostra remembers the URI and the command of the server that returned it, for up to 20,000 URIs (`MAX_EXTERNALS`). When Ostra remembers one more, it forgets the oldest.

`GET .../code/external?uri=` reads a remembered URI. Only these URIs are read, so the browser cannot name an arbitrary file. A URI that is empty or longer than 4,096 characters is an error. If no server named the URI since the Ostra server started, the route returns status 404, and the user must open the file again from the code that uses it. If the server entry left the settings, the route also returns 404.

The provider reads a `file://` URI from disk as UTF-8 text of at most 1 MiB. It reads a `jdt://` URI through the request `java/classFileContents`. Other schemes are not readable. A `usages` request with a `uri` and a 1-based `line` asks the server about the name in that outside file.

## Editor hints

The file editor sends the unsaved text and a cursor to the server over the WebSocket. The messages are `CodeComplete`, `CodeSignature`, and `CodeNavigate`. The answers are `CodeCompletion`, `CodeSignatureHelp`, and `CodeNavigation`. [Server, REST API, and WebSocket](server-and-api.md) describes the socket.

The socket keeps one running request for each kind. A newer request of a kind stops the older one, and the older one never answers. This is because the older cursor position is no longer current. Each socket queues at most 8 answers (`HINT_QUEUE`).

The server checks each hint request. The file must be inside the project. The text must be at most 1 MiB. The line must be inside the text. A `trigger` must be one character.

| Hint | Order of answers |
| --- | --- |
| Completion | Each language server in the order of the settings. The first answer wins. Then the index. |
| Signature help | Language servers only. The index has none to give. A failure returns status 502. |
| Jump to supertypes or implementations | The index first. Then language servers. |

The index answers a jump first because it is fast and holds every language that it parses. It answers only for a file that it holds and a name that it defines. Otherwise `navigate_index` returns nothing, and language servers can answer. A jump returns at most 50 locations (`MAX_NAVIGATION`).

The index completion is the fallback. `hint::from_index` lists up to 50 names (`MAX_INDEX_COMPLETIONS`) that start like the word at the cursor. It marks the list `incomplete`, so the editor asks again as the word grows. After a trigger character the list is empty, because the index does not know members. If a server fails, the answer from the index carries a warning that names the server.

## The file watcher

The watcher catches edits that Ostra tools do not make: a shell command, the editor of the user, or a checkout. Without it, the index catches up only at the 30-second check.

`code_watch::start` watches the project root and each folder that holds a listed file. It does not watch the whole tree, so ignored build folders add no watches. A new folder gets a watch when it appears. The watcher reads the ignore rules of `.gitignore` and `.git/info/exclude` in the project root, and it skips anything under `.git`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant FS as Disk
  participant W as code_watch thread
  participant S as on_outside_change
  participant I as Indexes
  participant L as LspPool
  participant B as Browser
  FS->>W: notify event
  W->>W: collect events until 250 ms of quiet or 2 s
  W->>S: OnBatch with Batch
  S->>I: touch for each changed path
  S->>L: touch sends didChangeWatchedFiles
  S->>B: ProjectFsChanged with paths
  B->>I: next query runs sync on touched paths
```

The watcher collects events into a `Batch` until 250 ms (`QUIET`) pass without an event, or until 2 seconds (`MAX_WAIT`) pass since the first event. A `Batch` holds the changed paths and a `structural` flag. A create, remove, or rename event sets `structural`. A data change does not.

`on_outside_change` then does three things. If the batch is structural, it drops the cached file list. It calls `Code::touch` for each changed path, which marks the path in the index and tells the running language servers. Then it pushes `ProjectFsChanged` on the channel `workspace:{id}`. If the batch holds more than 200 paths (`MAX_PUSHED_PATHS`), the path list is empty, and the browser reloads the whole listing.

The server starts the watcher on the first code request, hint, graph request, or tool call for a project. A watch on an old root is replaced when the root changes.

### Other sources of changes

Two other paths call `Code::touch`: the save of a file in the Files view (`announce_save`), and the write tools of an agent execution. After a touch, the next query reads the file again.

## Routes and limits

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/projects/{key}/code/file?path=` | `CodeFile` for one file. |
| `GET .../code/usages?symbol=&path=&line=&col=&limit=&uri=` | `CodeUsages`. A `uri` makes it an outside-file request. |
| `GET .../code/deps?path=` | `CodeDeps`. |
| `GET .../code/symbols?q=&limit=` | `CodeSymbols`. |
| `GET .../code/external?uri=` | `CodeExternalFile`. |
| `GET .../code/graph?package=&path=&symbol=&line=&depth=` | `CodeGraph`. |
| `POST .../code/reindex` | `CodeReindex`. |

The `symbol` value must have 1 to 256 characters (`MAX_SYMBOL_LEN`) with no whitespace and no control character. The error is "Name one symbol with symbol, such as `parse_config`." A `path` that names a folder gets "Name a file with path."

| Limit | Value | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| File size that Ostra tokenizes or indexes | 1 MiB | `MAX_FILE_BYTES` |
| Source bytes in one index | 256 MiB | `MAX_INDEX_BYTES` |
| Files that a usages query reads | 4,000 | `MAX_SCAN_FILES` |
| Importers in a deps answer | 2,000 | `MAX_IMPORTERS` |
| Full disk check of the index | 30 seconds | `FULL_SYNC` |
| Worker threads for analysis | the CPU count, at most 8 | `index::parallel` |
| Usages route limit | default 500, cap 2,000 | `DEFAULT_USAGES`, `MAX_USAGES` |
| Symbols route limit | default 50, cap 200 | `DEFAULT_SYMBOLS`, `MAX_SYMBOLS` |
| Output of a `code_provider` program | 64 MiB | `MAX_OUTPUT` |
| Items in a provider answer | 20,000 | `MAX_ITEMS` |
| Provider and language server timeout | default 10 seconds, 1 to 120 | `timeout_secs`, `MAX_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT` |
| Idle time before a server stops | 10 minutes | `IDLE` |
| Interval of the idle sweep | 60 seconds | `SWEEP` |
| Running language servers | 8 | `MAX_SERVERS` |
| Open documents for each server | 32 | `MAX_OPEN` |
| Age of an entry before a failed or dead server restarts | 30 seconds from the start of the entry | `RETRY` |
| Server `initialize` timeout | 60 seconds | `INIT_TIMEOUT` |
| Definitions for a name-only server query | 50 | `MAX_DEFINITIONS` |
| Remembered outside URIs | 20,000 | `MAX_EXTERNALS` |
| Wait for a starting server in a hint | 3 seconds | `HINT_WAIT` |
| Watcher quiet time and longest wait | 250 ms and 2 seconds | `QUIET`, `MAX_WAIT` |

## What happens when

- **The project is larger than the caps.** The index holds the files that fit and sets `truncated`. Usages, symbols, and graph answers say that some files are not searched.
- **A file is not in the index.** Usages, symbols, and the graph do not see it. A `file` answer still has colors and an outline, because `render` reads the text directly.
- **The same name has many definitions.** A name-only answer lists them all. A tool answer asks for `path`. The graph links none of them when a name has more than 3 defining files and no direct import.
- **A custom program fails.** The chain tries the language servers, then the index. The answer carries the failure as a warning.
- **The workspace file waits for approval.** The chain holds only the built-in provider, because `effective` clears `code_provider` and `language_servers`.
- **A language server starts slowly.** A request waits at most `timeout_secs`, and a hint waits 3 seconds. The server keeps starting. The answer or the fallback carries the message "`name` is still starting. Ask again in a moment." A server that loads the project makes answers carry a note that they can be incomplete.
- **A language server dies.** Requests pass to the next provider with the failure text. If the server died within 30 seconds of its start, the pool starts it again only after 30 seconds pass from its start. If the server ran longer than 30 seconds, the pool starts it again at the next request with no wait. The idle sweep also removes a stale entry.
- **The user changes a provider setting.** The next request builds a new chain. A server that started under other sandbox settings is replaced. A server that no longer appears in the settings stops at the idle sweep.
- **The watcher cannot start.** The server logs "outside edits reach the code index within 30 s". The index then catches up at the next full check. If the OS refuses some folders, the log names the count, and the periodic check covers them.
- **The Ostra server restarts.** The index, the language servers, and the outside URI list are empty. The first query builds the index again.
- **The user edits a file in the editor.** The index and the graph read the saved file on disk. Hints use the unsaved text that the editor sends.

## What code navigation does not guarantee

- The built-in index matches names. It has no type checker. A usages answer can include a mention of another symbol that has the same name, or miss a use through a value of an unknown type.
- A usages answer by meaning is a best guess. When the guess fails, the answer lists every use of the name.
- The dependency graph and the agent tools use only the built-in index. A language server or a custom program cannot improve them.
- Language servers and custom programs run project code and build scripts. The workspace sandbox limits them, but [Sandbox and egress proxy](sandbox.md) states what the sandbox does not guarantee.
- Files over 1 MiB, binary files, minified files, ignored files, and `Data` languages have no definitions in the index.
