Connections, `ready`, `login`, `callback`, `server_status`, and the tools of an execution.
The tool traits and the `run` function of the MCP tool.
`encrypt_with`, `VapidKeys`, and `Notifier::send`.
`ServerServices::notify`: reads the setting, finds the subscriptions, and sends the notices.
The `Services` trait that declares `notify`.
Browser subscription flow.

sections.title: Documentation books
sections.summary: How Ostra's docs stage writes a book per project set, how the engine validates, merges, stores, searches, shows, and exports it, and which limits and failure cases apply.
sections.body:
A documentation book keeps what one agent learned about a project, so the next agent does not read all the code again. Without a book, every task starts with a new search through files. Ostra solves this with a docs stage. In the stage, documentation agents describe each project, the engine merges the result into a book on disk, and later agents search the book before they read code.

This page covers these parts:

- The book model: parts, sections, sub-sections, the glossary, and the system architecture.
- The docs stage and the `WriteBook` step that ends it.
- The checks on a submit, including the caps on diagram size.
- The book ID and the merge by project set.
- The files that the engine writes.
- The `DocsSearch` tool, which ranks passages with BM25.
- The Docs screen, its search, and the HTML export.
- The API routes, the limits, and the failure cases.

The page [Sessions and the pipeline](sessions-and-pipeline.md) owns the planner and the closing gate. The page [Agents, prompts, and the spawn contract](agents-and-prompts.md) owns the spawn parameters and the repo brief. The page [Policy engine: guards and permissions](policy.md) owns the guards.

## The model of a book

A book covers a set of projects. Each project has one part, and a part holds an overview and a list of sections. A section holds the facts about one unit of work, such as a feature, a flow, or a component with one responsibility. A section can hold sub-sections. A sub-section has the same fields as a section but no sub-sections of its own, so the tree has two levels. A book of two or more projects can also hold one system architecture. All types live in [`crates/ostra-core/src/book.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/book.rs).

### Types

| Type | Fields | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Book` | `id`, `title`, `projects`, `updated_at`, `sessions`, `architecture`, `parts`, `glossary` | One book as `book.json` holds it. `projects` is sorted. `sessions` lists the sessions that wrote the book, oldest first. `glossary` is sorted by term. |
| `BookPart` | `project`, `overview`, `sections`, `updated_at` | One project's part. |
| `DocSection` | `id`, `title`, `purpose`, `boundaries`, `assumptions`, `business_flow`, `diagrams`, `tables`, `concerns`, `code_refs`, `subsections` | One unit of work. |
| `DocSubsection` | The fields of `DocSection` without `subsections` | One step or piece of a section that needs its own flow, diagram, or table. |
| `Boundaries` | `owns`, `does_not_own` | What the unit changes alone, and what it leaves to other units. |
| `BusinessStep` | `actor`, `action`, `outcome` | One step of the flow, in the words of the domain. |
| `DocTable` | `title`, `columns`, `rows` | A reference table. Each row has one cell per column. |
| `Concern` | `component`, `responsibility` | One row of the separation of concerns. |
| `CodeRef` | `path`, `symbol`, `lines`, `note` | A place in the code that the reader opens next. |
| `Diagram` | `title`, `kind`, `source` | A Mermaid diagram. `kind` is `sequence` or `flowchart`. |
| `GlossaryEntry` | `term`, `definition`, `code_ref` | One term. |
| `Architecture` | `overview`, `diagram`, `components`, `links`, `failure_recovery`, `scalability` | The architecture of a book of two or more projects. |
| `BookSummary` | `id`, `title`, `projects`, `updated_at`, `sections`, `has_architecture` | One row of the book list. `sections` counts the sections of all parts. |
| `BookUpdate` | `session`, `parts`, `architecture`, `glossary` | What one session adds to a book. The engine builds it from the event log. |

The architecture has four lists. A `Component` has a unique `name`, a `project` key (empty for an external system), a `role`, and `owns`. A `Link` has `from`, `to`, `protocol`, `mode` (`sync` or `async`), and `payload`. A `FailureCase` has `failure`, `detection`, and `recovery`. A `ScalingCase` has `component`, `scales_by`, and `limit`.

The Rust types derive `TS`, so the web console reads the same shapes from `web/src/api/gen`. See [The web console](web-console.md).

### Why every unit has assumptions

The `assumptions` list is required for every section and sub-section. It names each fact that the code takes as given without a check, such as an input shape or an environment variable. A reader or an agent that breaks an assumption breaks the code without a test failure. The check refuses an empty list. The writer can enter `None found in the code` only after it checks every input and caller.

## The docs stage

The docs stage is the last stage of a session that documents code. It has three parts: one documentation agent for each project, one system architecture agent for a book of two or more projects, and the `WriteBook` step. No agent writes a book file. Each agent returns its result in a submit call, and the engine writes every file (Rule B5).

### Flow of the stage

The planner in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/plan.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/plan.rs) decides each step. The functions `docs_stage` and `book_stage` hold the rules.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Closing stages reach a project"] --> B{"Docs on and no open BLOCKER?"}
  B -->|no| Z["The project has no part"]
  B -->|yes| C["Spawn documentation agent"]
  C --> D{"Submit readable?"}
  D -->|no| E["Failure gate: retry or abandon"]
  D -->|yes| F["Part is done"]
  F --> G{"Two or more parts?"}
  G -->|yes| H["Spawn system-architecture agent"]
  G -->|no| I["Step WriteBook"]
  H --> I
  I --> J["book::apply writes the files"]
```

### Steps in order

1. A session asks for documentation in one of two ways. The task has the `docs` option on, or the user answers the closing gate with docs on for a project. A session of category `Docs` skips the gate: the engine sets `closing` to `(false, true)` for each project in scope, which means no tests and docs on.
2. The planner starts the documentation agent for a project when its closing stages allow docs and its test stage is done. An open BLOCKER finding blocks documentation for that project (hard rule 21).
3. The planner starts at most `MAX_DOCS_WRITERS` (4) documentation agents at the same time. The count includes running agents and spawns that wait in the same planner pass.
4. The runner gives the agent one report per phase that passed. In a `Docs` session, no implementer ran. The runner then writes `ostra-docs-request.md` from the request text, and the report says that the agent must take the code to document from the request.
5. The agent returns a `DocumentationSubmit`. The engine stores it in the project track as `DocsState::Done`.
6. The function `book_progress` waits until every project has settled. A project is settled when its code is done and its docs are `Done` or `Abandoned`, or when it needs no docs. The function returns the list of projects with a finished part.
7. When two or more parts exist, the planner starts the system architecture agent. Before the spawn, the runner writes `ostra-docs-parts.json` in the session folder. The file maps each project key to its part as JSON. The agent runs in the session root with the projects in scope.
8. The planner pushes `Step::WriteBook` when the architecture is `Done` or `Abandoned`, or when only one part exists.
9. The runner takes a state snapshot, builds the `BookUpdate`, and calls `book::apply`. It then appends a `BookWritten` event with the book ID, the projects, and an error text when the write failed.
10. The session completes only after `book_written` is set, when at least one part exists. The `Documentation book` artifact points to the `index.md` of the book, but only when the write had no error.

The execution of the system architecture agent is recorded under the key of the first written project. The session view shows one card per project (`Documentation for <key>`), one `System architecture` card, and one `Book <id>` card that is `Done` or `Failed`.

### The two agents

| Agent | Tier | Timeout | Capabilities | Submit type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `documentation` | `advanced` | 2400 seconds | `read`, `shell`, `search_text`, `glob`, `code`, `docs_search` | `DocumentationSubmit` |
| `system-architecture` | `advanced` | 1800 seconds | `read`, `shell`, `search_text`, `glob`, `code`, `docs_search` | `ArchitectureSubmit` |

Both agents have the effort `high` on every executor. The prompts are in [`assets/agents/documentation/prompt.md`](assets/agents/documentation/prompt.md) and [`assets/agents/system-architecture/prompt.md`](assets/agents/system-architecture/prompt.md). The old name `module-documentation` still parses as `documentation`, so logs from before books still read.

The documentation agent gets these inputs: the implementer reports, the path of the existing `book.json` (when the book exists), the user notes for the docs stage, and the request text. The system architecture agent gets the parts file, the projects in scope, the existing `book.json`, and the user notes. The engine finds the existing book with `existing_book`, which uses `SessionState::book_id`.

The prompt of the documentation agent sets these rules:

- The submit replaces the whole previous part of the project. A section that the agent leaves out is removed from the book.
- After a build, the agent rewrites the sections that the changed files reach and copies the other sections unchanged.
- The agent writes in plain literal English. It names the real type, route, and config key, and it writes no metaphor.
- The agent writes no file. The write guard refuses a write under the books folder.

The system architecture agent must verify each link between projects in source before it lists the link. It must also state when the code and the deployment files do nothing to recover from a failure.

### What happens when

- **A run ends without a readable submit.** The state is `Failed` with the text `The run ended without a readable submit call, so there is nothing to put in the book.` The planner opens an execution-failed gate. See [Judges, gates, and YOLO mode](gates-and-judges.md). If the user answers retry, the state returns to `NotStarted` and the agent runs again. Otherwise the state is `Abandoned`.
- **A run is interrupted** by a pause or a restart. The state returns to `NotStarted`, and the planner starts the agent again.
- **A BLOCKER finding is open** for a project. The project has no part. The book waits for no part from it.
- **A part is abandoned.** The book is named after the parts that were written. If no part remains, no book is written and the session completes without a book.
- **Only one project is documented.** The planner starts no architecture agent.
- **The architecture is abandoned.** The engine writes the book without a new architecture. The old architecture, if any, stays in the book.
- **The disk write fails.** `BookWritten.error` holds `The book could not be written to <dir>: <cause>`. The book card is `Failed`, no artifact appears, and the session still completes.

## What the engine checks in a submit

Both executors call `validate_submit` when an agent calls its submit tool. For the two docs agents, the function runs `check_documentation` or `check_architecture`. If any issue exists, the tool refuses the call and returns every issue, one per line. Each issue starts with the correction. The agent fixes the issues and calls the tool again. When `status` is not `ok`, for example `stuck`, the checks do not run.

### Rules for a documentation submit

| Check | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Sections | `sections` has at least one entry, because the book shows only what the agent submits. |
| Title and purpose | Each section and sub-section has a non-empty title and a non-empty `purpose`. |
| Assumptions | Each section and sub-section has at least one non-empty assumption (Rule B2). |
| IDs | Each ID is a slug: it starts with a lowercase letter or a digit, has at most 64 characters, and holds only lowercase letters, digits, and dashes. |
| Unique IDs | No ID is used twice across all sections and sub-sections of the submit. |
| Tables | Each table has columns, and each row has one cell per column. |
| Code references | Each `path` is relative: not empty, no leading `/`, `\\`, or `~`, no drive letter such as `C:`, and no `..` component. |
| Diagrams | The kind matches the first line, and the size is within the caps (Rule B3). |
| Glossary | Each entry has a term and a definition, and no term appears twice when case is ignored. |

### Rules for an architecture submit

- The `architecture` field is present when `status` is `ok`.
- The overview is not empty.
- The diagram has kind `flowchart` and is within the node cap.
- The list of components has at least two entries with unique names.
- Each link names a listed component at both ends, and the list of links is not empty.
- `failure_recovery` and `scalability` each have at least one entry.
- The glossary follows the same rules as in a documentation submit.

## Diagram caps

A documentation submit can hold diagrams of two kinds only: `sequence` and `flowchart`. The caps keep a diagram small, because a reader follows a small diagram and loses a large one (Rule B3). The check `check_diagram` ignores empty lines and `%%` comments.

| Cap | Constant | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Participants in a sequence diagram | `MAX_SEQUENCE_PARTICIPANTS` | 8 |
| Messages in a sequence diagram | `MAX_SEQUENCE_MESSAGES` | 20 |
| Nodes in a flowchart | `MAX_FLOWCHART_NODES` | 15 |

The check counts like this:

- A sequence diagram must start with `sequenceDiagram`. The function `sequence_size` builds one set of participant names. It adds each name that a `participant` or `actor` line declares (the part before ` as `). It also adds the name on both sides of each arrow (`from` and `to`). A name that appears in both places counts once.
- A message is a line with an arrow and a colon. The check knows the arrows `->>`, `-->>`, `->`, `-->`, `-x`, `--x`, `-)`, `--)`, `<<->>`, and `<<-->>`.
- A flowchart must start with `flowchart` or `graph`. The check removes node shapes, edge labels, and edges, and counts the distinct node IDs that remain. It skips the lines that start with `subgraph`, `end`, `style`, `classDef`, `class`, `linkStyle`, `click`, or `direction`.
- If the kind and the first line disagree, the issue says which first line the kind needs.
- If a diagram is too large, the issue tells the agent to split it into one diagram per step.

## Book ID and merge by project set

A book is named by its project set, so a later session on the same projects updates the same book (Rule B6). The function `book_id` sorts the keys, removes duplicates, and joins them with `_`. For `web` and `api` the ID is `api_web`. Project keys contain no `_`, so two different sets never give the same ID.

An ID has at most `MAX_BOOK_ID` (80) characters. For a longer name, `book_id` cuts the text at a character boundary, then adds `_` and a 16-digit hexadecimal FNV-1a hash of the full name. The function `is_book_id` accepts an ID that starts with a lowercase letter or a digit, has at most 80 characters, and holds only lowercase letters, digits, `-`, and `_`. The API and the folder scan use it, so a name like `../x` never reaches the file system.

The user can pick a book on the New task screen. When the `docs` toggle is on, a list shows `Book: new or matching the projects` and each existing book. The screen sends `docs_book` in the `CreateSession` body only when the toggle is on and a book is picked. `Engine::create_session` refuses a bad ID with `Pick a documentation book from the list instead of ...`. A valid ID of a book that does not exist yet creates a book with that ID.

### Merge rules

The function `merge` combines the existing book with a `BookUpdate`:

1. A project's new part replaces its old part. Parts of other projects stay.
2. Parts are sorted by project key.
3. A new architecture replaces the old one. When the update has no architecture, the old one stays.
4. Glossary entries merge by term. The comparison trims the term and ignores case. The newer definition wins. The list is sorted by lowercase term.
5. `projects` is the sorted set of project keys of all parts. `title` is `Documentation for ` and the keys, joined with `, `.
6. The session ID is added to `sessions` when it is not there. `updated_at` is the time of the merge.

The function `apply` reads the book, merges, and writes it. It holds `BOOK_LOCK`, a process-wide mutex, for the whole read-merge-write. `remove` takes the same lock. Because of the lock, two sessions that update one book at the same time keep the parts of each other. A test starts 8 threads that each add one part, and the book keeps all 8 parts and all 8 sessions. If both sessions write the same project, the later merge wins.

## Files that the engine writes

The function `write` creates the folder `.ostra/docs/<book id>/` in the workspace root. The path comes from `dir` and `book_dir`. It writes these files:

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `book.json` | The whole `Book` as pretty JSON. The API serves this file. |
| `index.md` | The title, the update time in UTC, a link to the glossary, a link to the architecture when it exists, then for each project its overview and one bullet per section with the first sentence of its purpose. |
| `glossary.md` | A table with the columns Term, Definition, and Code. |
| `architecture.md` | The overview, the diagram, and the tables Components, Communication, Failure and recovery, and Scalability. The file exists only when the book has an architecture. |
| `<project>/<section id>.md` | One section with its sub-sections. |

A section file starts with `# <title>` and `Project: <key>`. It then holds the purpose, and these parts in a fixed order (Rule B1): Boundaries (Owns, Does not own), Assumptions, Business flow as a table, the diagrams, the tables, Separation of concerns, and Code references. A sub-section is a `##` part with the same order one level lower. The engine test checks that code references come after the first diagram.

After the write, `remove_stale` deletes each file that the write did not produce and each empty folder. A section that a new part leaves out loses its file. The folder never holds a stale file.

### Who can write the folder

Only the engine writes the books (Rule B5). Three layers enforce this:

- The guard `workspace-docs` in the policy denies any agent write, move, or delete under the books folder. The message tells the agent to put the documentation in its submit call.
- The sandbox profile adds the books folder as a read-only directory. See [Sandbox and egress proxy](sandbox.md).
- The API deletes a book only through `DELETE /api/workspaces/{ws}/docs/{book}`.

## Search for agents with BM25

An agent that has the `docs_search` capability calls the `DocsSearch` tool. The tool is in [`crates/ostra-tools/src/misc.rs`](crates/ostra-tools/src/misc.rs), and the ranking is in [`crates/ostra-core/src/book_search.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/book_search.rs). The repo brief lists up to `MAX_BRIEF_BOOKS` (20) books and tells such an agent to search before it reads code. The brief also warns that a book describes the code when it was written, so the agent must check each fact against the code. See [Agents, prompts, and the spawn contract](agents-and-prompts.md).

### Tool input

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string, required | The question, with any names that the agent knows. |
| `project` | string | A project key. The tool then searches only that part of the books. |
| `limit` | integer | Hits to return. The default is `DEFAULT_LIMIT` (5). The tool clamps it to 1 through `MAX_LIMIT` (15). |

The tool searches all books of the workspace. It has no filter for one book. For each call, it loads every readable `book.json`, builds the index in a blocking task, and ranks the passages. The tool keeps no cache. The reply is `N section(s) matched, most relevant first`, then one block for each hit with its place, its file path, and the passages that matched.

These replies need no ranking:

- The run has no workspace: the tool says that no books exist and tells the agent to read the code.
- The workspace has no books: the tool says so.
- No passage matches: the tool says that no section matches and suggests other names.

### Units and passages

The index has units and passages. A unit is a part of a book that a hit points to. A passage is a small piece of text of a unit.

| Unit | Unit ID | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overview of a part | `project/overview` | `index.md` |
| Section | `project/section` | `project/section.md` |
| Sub-section | `project/section/sub` | The file of its section. |
| Glossary term | `glossary/term` | `glossary.md` |
| Architecture aspect: overview, components, communication, failure, scalability | `architecture/aspect` | `architecture.md` |

The builder cuts each section into passages: each paragraph of the purpose, the boundaries, the assumptions, the business flow, each diagram, the rows of each table, the concerns, and the code references. Lists and tables go in windows of `WINDOW` (5) items or rows. A diagram passage keeps only its labels and messages, without Mermaid keywords and words of 2 characters or less, so a search for `participant` finds nothing.

### Ranking

The ranking steps are:

1. The tokenizer `tokens` splits the query on characters that are not letters, digits, or `_`. It splits an identifier at camelCase and snake_case borders and keeps the whole identifier too, so `SessionState::fold` gives `sessionstate`, `session`, `state`, and `fold`. It converts text to lowercase, drops one-character words and stop words, and applies the function `stem` to each word. The stemmer has three rules, and the first rule that fits wins:
   - If the word is longer than 4 characters and ends in `ies`, `ies` becomes `y`.
   - If the word is longer than 4 characters and ends in `sses`, `sses` becomes `ss`.
   - If the word is longer than 3 characters and does not end in `ss`, `us`, or `is`, the trailing `s` is removed.
2. Each passage has three fields with weights: the label has `W_TITLE` (2.0), the paths and symbols of code references have `W_CODE` (1.5), and the body has `W_BODY` (1.0).
3. The passage score is BM25 with `K1` 1.2 and `B` 0.75. The term frequency is the weighted sum over the three fields. The IDF is `ln(1 + (n - df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5))`, where `n` is the count of passages and units.
4. The score of a unit is its title score plus its best passage plus `SECOND_SHARE` (0.35) of its second-best passage. The title counts once for the unit and never picks the passages that the hit shows.
5. A hit shows at most `PASSAGES_PER_HIT` (2) passages. A passage below `SHOW_SHARE` (0.5) of the best one is hidden. When only the title matched, the hit shows the first passage.
6. The tool sorts hits by score, then by unit order, and cuts the list at the limit.

The tests in `book_search.rs` check that a query like `how many executions run concurrently` finds the section `Execution slots` with only its matching passage, and that a query for a path like `auth.rs` finds the section whose code references hold the path.

## The Docs screen

The console shows books in two screens in [`web/src/screens/DocsScreen.tsx`](web/src/screens/DocsScreen.tsx). See [The web console](web-console.md) for the shell and the routes.

### The book list

`DocsScreen` is the resource `ws:docs` at `/w/:ws/docs`. It calls `api.books` and shows a table with the columns Book, Projects, Sections, Architecture, and Updated. The list is newest first. A click on a row opens the resource `book:<id>`. When the list is empty, the screen says `No books yet. Start a task that asks for documentation to write the first one.`

### The book reader

`BookScreen` is the resource `book:<id>` at `/w/:ws/b/:id`. It loads the book with `api.book` and renders it with the `BookReader`. The reader has a title bar with the search box, the `Export HTML` button, and the `Delete` button. Below the bar are three columns: the contents, the page, and the list `On this page`.

The module [`web/src/features/docs/bookModel.ts`](web/src/features/docs/bookModel.ts) turns the `Book` JSON into Markdown pages. It does not read the Markdown files that the engine writes. The function `bookPages` builds the pages, and `bookDocs` wraps them in the `Docs` model for the renderer. The pages are in this order:

1. `overview`: the title, the projects, the update time, a table of section counts per project, and the overview of each part.
2. `glossary`: only when the book has glossary entries.
3. `architecture`: only when the book has an architecture.
4. One page for each section, with the ID `<project>.<section id>`. The nav groups them under the project key. A project without sections has no group.

The nav lists the sub-sections of a section under the page of the section. The pager at the bottom of a page links to the previous and the next page. The `On this page` list follows the scroll position: the active entry is the last heading that is at most 96 pixels above the top of the pane. The page shows the code references as a table with the path prefixed by the project key.

### Safe rendering of book text

Book text comes from an agent, so the model escapes it. A title or a term shows as the characters that it holds (`inlineText`). A table cell stays on one line, and `|` is escaped (`cell`). A line of prose cannot start a heading, a code fence, or a thematic break (`prose`). A code span holds any backticks in its text (`code`). The renderer never shows raw HTML. The unit tests and the browser test check that `<script>` text and an `<img onerror>` term stay plain text.

A `mermaid` block draws as SVG in [`design/src/docs/Diagram.tsx`](design/src/docs/Diagram.tsx). Mermaid loads only on a page that has a diagram. It runs in `strict` mode with `htmlLabels` off, so a diagram cannot hold an image or leave the page. The code removes links from the SVG. A diagram that does not parse shows its source. See [The design system](design-system.md).

### Search in the Docs screen

The screen has its own search, which is different from the BM25 search of the agents. It runs in the browser on the pages of one book. It starts when the query has at least `MIN_QUERY` (2) characters. The match is a case-insensitive substring. The model indexes the page titles (rank 0), the headings (rank 1), and the text blocks (rank 2), and keeps one hit for each page section. Hits sort by rank. The list shows at most `MAX_HITS` (80) hits and adds `+` to the count when it reaches 80. A hit shows 48 characters before the match and 90 after.

### Delete a book

Copy the folder `.ostra/docs/<book id>/` before you delete a book. The delete removes every file in the folder and cannot be undone.

The `Delete` button opens a dialog with the text that the next documentation task on the same projects writes a new book. The button `Delete the book` calls `DELETE /api/workspaces/{ws}/docs/{book}`. After success, the screen opens the list and closes the book tab. After a failure, the dialog shows the error.

## HTML export

The button `Export HTML` makes one HTML file of the whole book in the browser. The code is in [`web/src/features/docs/exportHtml.ts`](web/src/features/docs/exportHtml.ts). The file name is `<book id>.html`.

### Steps of the export

1. The reader renders every page into a hidden element with `aria-hidden`.
2. `diagramsDrawn` waits until each diagram has an SVG, or for at most 15000 milliseconds. After the timeout, the export continues with what exists.
3. `buildExportHtml` creates a new document with DOM calls, so no book text is parsed as markup. It adds a table of contents, grouped like the nav, and each page in reading order. It keeps the theme of the console (`light` or `dark`).
4. `clean` removes what the renderer never makes but a file must not carry.
5. `download` saves the file with a temporary object URL.

The cleaning step does these actions:

- It removes the elements `script`, `iframe`, `object`, `embed`, `frame`, `frameset`, `link`, `meta`, `base`, `form`, `input`, `button`, `foreignObject`, `audio`, `video`, and `source`.
- It removes each attribute that starts with `on`.
- It keeps a `src` attribute only when its value starts with `data:image/`.
- It keeps an `href` only when its value starts with `#`, `http:`, `https:`, or `mailto:`.
- It prefixes each element ID with the page ID and rewrites the internal links to match.
- It adds `rel="noreferrer"` to each external link.

The file has its own meta policy: `default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:`. It loads nothing and runs nothing. The Playwright test in [`tests/browser/specs/books.spec.ts`](tests/browser/specs/books.spec.ts) opens an exported file and checks these facts: no `script`, `iframe`, `object`, `embed`, or `foreignObject` tag, no inline event handler, the exact policy text, all pages in order, the diagrams already drawn, and no script in the document. See [Tests and evals](testing.md).

If the export fails, the screen shows `The book could not be exported: <error>` in a banner. The button is disabled while an export runs.

## API routes for books

| Route | Handler | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/docs` | `books_list` | A list of `BookSummary`, newest first. A folder with an invalid name or an unreadable `book.json` is skipped. |
| `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/docs/{book}` | `book_get` | The `Book`. The status is 404 with `No such book in this workspace.` when the book is missing. |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{ws}/docs/{book}` | `book_delete` | The list of the remaining books. |

An ID that fails `is_book_id` gets status 400. A delete gets status 404 when `book.json` is missing. It gets status 409 with `Try again in a moment, because work is starting in this workspace.` when the workspace work lock is busy, so no session starts between the check and the removal (Rule W4). A failed removal gets status 500. See [Server, REST API, and WebSocket](server-and-api.md).

## Survey, page, and synthesis steps

The code in this repository has no survey, page, or synthesis step. The type `DocumentationSubmit` has the fields `status`, `summary`, `overview`, `sections`, `glossary`, and `stuck`, and no `step` field. One documentation agent returns the whole part of one project in one submit. The engine does not plan pages, does not start one writer for each page, and does not run a synthesis pass. Its only fan-out is one agent for each project, with the cap `MAX_DOCS_WRITERS`. The sections of a part come from the single writer.

## Limits

| Limit | Name | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Documentation agents at the same time | `MAX_DOCS_WRITERS` | 4 |
| Documentation agent timeout | `timeout_seconds` in `agent.toml` | 2400 seconds |
| System architecture agent timeout | `timeout_seconds` in `agent.toml` | 1800 seconds |
| Book ID length | `MAX_BOOK_ID` | 80 characters |
| Section ID length | `is_slug` | 64 characters |
| Sequence diagram | `MAX_SEQUENCE_PARTICIPANTS`, `MAX_SEQUENCE_MESSAGES` | 8 participants, 20 messages |
| Flowchart | `MAX_FLOWCHART_NODES` | 15 nodes |
| Search limit | `DEFAULT_LIMIT`, `MAX_LIMIT` | 5 by default, 15 at most |
| Passage window | `WINDOW` | 5 items or rows |
| Passages for each hit | `PASSAGES_PER_HIT` | 2 |
| Books in the repo brief | `MAX_BRIEF_BOOKS` | 20 |
| Docs screen hits | `MAX_HITS` | 80 |
| Docs screen minimum query | `MIN_QUERY` | 2 characters |
| Wait for diagrams in an export | `timeoutMs` of `diagramsDrawn` | 15000 milliseconds |

No user setting changes these values. The constants are in the code.

## What books do not guarantee

- A book describes the code when the agent wrote it. The code can change after that, and no step updates a book unless a new docs stage runs.
- The engine checks the form of a submit and not its truth. The checks cannot find a wrong name, a wrong number, or a link that does not exist. The prompts require grounding in the code, but no code verifies it.
- A project that a session does not document keeps its old part. A part can be old next to a new one.
- A part is replaced as a whole. If a writer leaves out a section by mistake, the book loses that section.
- A `book.json` that fails to parse reads as no book. The next merge then starts a new book from the update alone and removes the other files of the folder.
- A change of the project set makes a new book ID, and the old book stays on disk until a user deletes it.
- A book is workspace data under `.ostra/docs/`. It is not a part of the project repository.

sections.title: The web console
sections.summary: How the React app in web/ boots, routes, shows screens on desktop and phone, talks to the server over REST and /ws, and ships inside the release ostra binary.
sections.body:
The web console is the only user interface of Ostra. Without it, a user cannot answer a gate, watch an execution, or read an artifact. The console is a React 19 single-page app in `web/`. It has no server-side logic. It reads state from the REST API and from one WebSocket, and it sends user decisions back with REST calls. A release build of the `ostra` binary embeds the compiled app and serves it.

This page covers the code in `web/src`: boot, routes, the desktop shell, the mobile shell, the screens, the API client, the socket, the shared stores, the generated types, the mock API, shortcuts, the command palette, and the build. The REST routes and the `/ws` protocol belong to [Server, REST API, and WebSocket](server-and-api.md). The component library belongs to [The design system](design-system.md). The test layers belong to [Tests and evals](testing.md).

## Source layout

The root `package.json` lists three npm workspaces: `design`, `web`, and `site`. The `site/` folder is not in the working tree of this repository, so `npm` commands in this repository cover `design/` and `web/` only. `web/` imports the shared components from `@ostra/design`.

| Folder in `web/src` | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `main.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `auth.ts` | Boot, the route table, and the sign-in token exchange. |
| `api/` | `client.ts` (REST), `socket.ts` (WebSocket), `gen/` (generated types), `types.ts`, `nav.ts`, `extra.ts`, and `mock/` (fixtures). |
| `shell/` | The desktop chrome: `WorkspaceShell.tsx`, `TitleBar.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx`, `StatusBar.tsx`, `QuickDock.tsx`, `Palette.tsx`, `ResizeHandle.tsx`, `Home.tsx`, and `SignIn.tsx`. |
| `screens/` | One component for each kind of resource, plus `setup/` for onboarding and dialogs. `screens/README.md` lists the props of each screen. |
| `mobile/` | `MobileShell.tsx`, `Sheets.tsx`, and the phone screens in `mobile/screens/`. |
| `lib/` | Tabs, resource ids, shortcuts, the palette model, live stores, theme, install, push, and event folding. |
| `features/` | Code that several screens share: `gates/` (gate cards), `context/` (file tags and uploads), and `docs/` (book model and HTML export). |
| `components/` | `Markdown.tsx` and the Monaco setup in `monaco.ts`. |
| `content/` | Text tables for agents and stages. |

## Boot sequence

`main.tsx` runs `boot()` before it renders. The order matters because the sign-in token must leave the address bar before any request runs.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["boot() in main.tsx"] --> B["watchInstall()"]
  B --> C{"isMock?"}
  C -- yes --> F["render App"]
  C -- no --> D["exchangeTokenFromUrl()"]
  D --> E["watchForTokens() and registerServiceWorker()"]
  E --> F
  F --> G{"a request returned 401?"}
  G -- yes --> H["SignIn screen"]
  G -- no --> I["RouterProvider"]
```

- `exchangeTokenFromUrl()` reads `#token=` from the URL hash. It removes the hash with `history.replaceState` before it calls `api.exchange`. The token then stays out of the browser history and out of copied links.
- If the browser prerenders the page, the function waits for the `prerenderingchange` event. A prerender must not spend the one-time token.
- The `exchanged` `Set` in `web/src/auth.ts` stops a repeated exchange of the same token. `boot()` in `web/src/main.tsx` is the only caller of `exchangeTokenFromUrl()`, and it runs once before `createRoot(...).render`.
- `watchForTokens()` reloads the page when a new `#token=` hash appears. A hash change does not reload the page, so the boot-time exchange never sees the new hash.
- `onUnauthorized` listeners run for each response with status 401. `App` then renders `SignIn`. The user pastes the link that `ostra` printed. `tokenFromInput` accepts a full link or a bare token of 16 or more hex characters.

The server side of the token and the cookie belongs to [Sign-in, host checks, and secrets](auth-and-secrets.md).

## Routes and resource ids

The route table is the `routes` array in `App.tsx`. The app and the tests use the same array. The tests pass it to `createMemoryRouter`.

| Path | Element |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | `Home`: the first-run setup, or the workspace list. |
| `/w/:ws` | `WorkspaceShell`, with child routes for `cost`, `settings`, `memory`, `skills`, `docs`, `b/:id`, `s/:id`, `x/:id`, `artifact`, `p/:key`, and `f/:key/*`. Each child renders `RouteScreen`. |
| `/w/:ws/projects` | `ProjectsRedirect`: goes to the workspace overview. Projects open one for each tab. |
| `/s/:id` | `SessionRedirect`: loads the session to find its workspace, then redirects. Push notifications use this link. |
| `/x/:id` | `ExecutionRedirect`: finds the workspace through the session of the execution. It shows "This execution belongs to no session." when there is none. |
| `/_design` | The design gallery. The route exists only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true. |
| `*` | `NotFound`. |

Everything the console can open in a tab has a **resource id**. `lib/resource.ts` defines the ids. It maps each id to one URL and each URL back to one id. A reload or a deep link therefore restores the same tab.

| Resource id | URL | Screen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ws:overview` | `/w/:ws` | `WorkspaceScreen` |
| `ws:cost`, `ws:settings`, `ws:memory`, `ws:skills`, `ws:docs` | `/w/:ws/<page>` | `CostScreen`, `SettingsScreen`, `MemoryScreen`, `SkillsScreen`, `DocsScreen` |
| `book:<id>` | `/w/:ws/b/:id` | `BookScreen` |
| `session:<id>` | `/w/:ws/s/:id` | `SessionScreen` |
| `exec:<id>` | `/w/:ws/x/:id` | `ExecutionScreen` |
| `artifact:<path>` | `/w/:ws/artifact?path=<path>` | `ArtifactScreen` |
| `project:<key>` | `/w/:ws/p/:key` | `ProjectScreen` |
| `file:<key>:<path>` | `/w/:ws/f/:key/<path>` | `FileScreen` |
| `dep:<key>:<uri>` | `/w/:ws/d/:key?uri=<uri>` | `DependencyFileScreen` |

The parser splits `file:` and `dep:` ids at the first colon after the project key. A project key never contains a colon, but a path or a URI can. The `d/:key` route has no entry of its own in `routes`. The catch-all `*` child of `/w/:ws` handles it. An `anchor` becomes the URL hash. Examples are `#gate-<id>` on a session, `#setting:<dotted key>` on settings, and `#lesson:<key>:<id>` on memory.

## Desktop shell

`WorkspaceShell` chooses between two shells with `useIsMobile()`. It renders `MobileShell` or `Shell`. It sets `key={ws}`, so a switch to another workspace remounts the shell. Tabs, stores, and dialogs never leak from one workspace into another.

`Shell` draws the title bar, the sidebar, the tab strip, the center pane, the quick-question dock, and the status bar. It owns four kinds of state:

- **Tabs.** A `useReducer` with `tabsReducer` from `lib/tabs.ts`.
- **Layout preferences (`UiPrefs`).** `leftTab` (`sessions`, `files`, `artifacts`, or `git`), `filesProject`, `sidebarOpen`, `dockOpen`, and `theme`. The defaults are in `DEFAULT_PREFS`: sessions tab, sidebar open, dock closed, theme from the system.
- **Dialogs.** One of `new-workspace`, `add-project`, or `setup`.
- **Panel widths.** The hook `usePanelWidths()` in `shell/ResizeHandle.tsx` returns the widths of the sidebar and the dock.

The widths are not part of the workspace layout.

### Panel widths

`usePanelWidths()` returns a pair: the `PanelWidths` object (`sidebar` and `dock`, in pixels) and a setter. The hook stores the widths in `localStorage` under the key `ostra.panels`. It writes the value after each change and reads it when the shell mounts. The widths stay in this browser because they depend on the screen, not on the workspace.

The defaults are 264 px for the sidebar and 380 px for the dock. The setter limits the sidebar to 180 to 640 px and the dock to 260 to 900 px. If storage is unavailable, the widths apply until the page reloads.

`Shell` writes the widths into the `style` of its root `div` as the CSS variables `--sidebar-w` and `--dock-w`. `Sidebar.tsx` and `QuickDock.tsx` read them with `var(--sidebar-w)` and `var(--dock-w)`. A `ResizeHandle` on the edge of each panel calls the setter during a drag.

### Context that the shell gives to screens

The shell gives each screen three React contexts through `ConsoleContext`: `useNav()`, `useShell()`, and `useWorkspace()`. A screen never changes tabs directly. It calls `useNav().open(id, { preview, anchor, beside })`. The context value is the contract between the shell and the screens. The mobile shell supplies the same shape.

### Tabs follow the URL and the URL follows the tabs

The URL and the active tab must always name the same resource. Two effects in `Shell` keep them equal:

1. When `routeId` changes, the shell dispatches `activate`. This covers the Back button and typed links.
2. When `tabs.active` changes, the shell calls `navigate(resourcePath(ws, active, anchor))`.

The ref `shellNav` marks a URL change that the shell made itself. Without the ref, step 2 triggers step 1, and the two effects loop. The center pane shows `<Outlet />`. `RouteScreen` reads the URL, not the tab list, and calls `ScreenFor`. If no tab is open, the pane shows `NothingOpen`. If `api.workspace` fails, the pane shows `WorkspaceMissing`.

### Tab rules

`lib/tabs.ts` is a pure reducer. Its rules are:

- At most one tab is the **preview tab**, shown in italics. A list row opens with `{ preview: true }` and replaces the current preview tab. An explicit action opens a normal tab.
- A double click on a tab or on the pane runs `keep`, which turns a preview tab into a normal tab. A plain `open` of an existing preview tab does the same.
- **Pinned** tabs sit before all other tabs. They are never preview tabs. Bulk closes (`closeMany` with scope `all`, `others`, `left`, or `right`) skip them. `move` keeps a tab inside its own group.
- When the active tab closes, its right neighbor becomes active. If it has none, the left neighbor becomes active.
- `activate` adds a tab that is not open. A deep link therefore always shows a tab.
- `normalizeTabs` drops duplicate ids and extra preview tabs, puts pinned tabs first, and points `active` at an open tab. Every restore runs it, because the user can edit stored layouts.

A middle click closes a tab. A vertical mouse wheel over the strip scrolls it sideways. The shell registers this listener as a native non-passive listener, because the React `onWheel` handler is passive and cannot call `preventDefault`.

### Layout storage

The layout lives in two places, so a new browser gets the layout of an old one.

- **Local copy:** `localStorage` key `ostra.ui.<ws>`, written after every change. It loads first and gives an instant layout.
- **Server copy:** `GET /api/workspaces/:ws/ui` (`api.uiState`) and `PATCH` (`api.patchUiState`) with a `WorkspaceUiState`. The shell sends the PATCH 800 ms after the last change (`PATCH_DELAY_MS`). It sends nothing until the first GET finishes. An early PATCH overwrites the server copy with an empty layout.

The shell restores the server copy only when this browser has no local copy. `fromServerUi` returns `null` for an empty stored state. The shell ignores a failed GET or PATCH, and the local copy stays valid.

### Other desktop parts

- **Quick-question dock** (`QuickDock.tsx`): calls `api.ask(ws, { question, session })`, then follows `execution:<id>` for the streamed answer. "Turn into task" stores the text in `taskDraft` and opens the New task form.
- **Status bar** (`StatusBar.tsx`): shows the socket state, running executions, open gates, and spend from `useActivity(ws)`. The label reads `Live · <host>`, `Connecting`, or `Offline, reconnecting`. In mock mode it reads `Mock data`.
- **Live favicon** (`markState.ts`): the browser tab icon shows eight arcs, one for each board lane, for the session of the active tab. The arcs before the current lane are done.
- **Pending commands notice:** `PendingCommandsNotice` shows when `WorkspaceDetail.pending_commands` is not empty, unless the settings tab is active. The approval rules belong to [Workspaces, projects, and approvals](workspaces-and-trust.md).
- **Home** (`/`): shows the onboarding wizard when `api.onboarding()` reports no `onboarded_at` and zero workspaces. Otherwise it lists the workspaces from `useWorkspaces()`.

## Screens

`screens/index.tsx` exports `ScreenFor({ ws, id })`. It parses the id and returns one screen. Each screen has the key `id`, so each tab starts with fresh state. `screens/README.md` holds the full props table. The summary is:

| Screen | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `WorkspaceScreen` | The New task form and the sessions table. It reads and clears `useShell().taskDraft`. |
| `SessionScreen` | The session board: lanes, gates, decisions, and the event log. |
| `ExecutionScreen` | A usage strip, then the Activity stream or the Terminal, chosen by `ExecutionView.stream`. |
| `ArtifactScreen` | A spec, plan, report, or review ledger. |
| `SettingsScreen` | The workspace settings forms, MCP servers, sandbox panels, and the Shortcuts tab. |
| `CostScreen` | Spend tables for this week (from `WorkspaceActivity.week_since`) or for all time. |
| `MemoryScreen`, `SkillsScreen` | Lessons and skills for each project. |
| `DocsScreen`, `BookScreen` | The documentation books and one book. See [Documentation books](documentation-books.md). |
| `ProjectScreen` | The project header, the Overview or Initialize flow, the Commands panel, and the Dependencies graph. |
| `FileScreen`, `DependencyFileScreen` | A project file in the Monaco editor, or a read-only dependency file. |
| `setup/Onboarding`, `NewWorkspaceDialog`, `AddProjectDialog` | The first-run wizard and the two dialogs. |

Two rules from `screens/index.tsx` and the README apply to every new screen:

- **Scrolling.** `selfScrolling(id)` returns true for ids that start with `artifact:`, `file:`, `dep:`, `project:`, or `book:`. The shell gives those screens the whole pane with `overflow: hidden`. Every other screen scrolls inside the pane.
- **Lazy heavy libraries.** The Monaco diff (`artifact/MonacoDiff.tsx`), the file editor (`project/code/FileEditor.tsx`), and xterm (`execution/XtermScreen.tsx`) load with `lazy()`. Import them only through their lazy wrapper, because a direct import moves the library into the main chunk. Monaco is set up in `components/monaco.ts`. That file imports only the editor contributions that the console uses and no language workers.

The gate cards in `features/gates/` render each `GatePayload` kind. `lib/gateAnswers.ts` maps each gate kind to the answer kind that the engine accepts (`ANSWER_KIND`). That table mirrors `runner::validate_answer` in the engine. Change the two together. The gate rules belong to [Judges, gates, and YOLO mode](gates-and-judges.md).

## Mobile shell

`useIsMobile()` is true when the media query `(max-width: 720px)` matches. It follows rotation and window resizes. It is always false in the homepage shot build. `MobileShell` replaces the tabs, the sidebar, the dock, and the status bar with one stack of screens:

- **Header.** A back button (when `canBack`), the title and subtitle from `mobileTitle()`, and buttons for search, a quick question, and the menu. On the overview, the workspace mark opens the workspace menu.
- **Sheets.** `MenuSheet`, `SearchSheet`, and `AskSheet` in `Sheets.tsx` slide over the screen. They are the mobile forms of the menu, the palette, and the dock.
- **Footer.** The socket state (`Live`, `Connecting`, `Offline`, or `Mock data`), the running count, the first open gate, and the spend of today.
- **Setup.** `MSetup` shows onboarding, a new workspace, or an added project inside the stack, with the modes `onboard`, `new`, and `add`.

`MobileScreenFor` maps a resource id to a phone screen: `MHome`, `MWorkspace` (cost, memory, skills), `MSettings`, `MSession`, `MExecution`, `MArtifact`, and `MProject` (for both `project:` and `file:`). It reuses the desktop `DocsScreen`, `BookScreen`, and `DependencyFileScreen`. The mobile shell supplies the same `ConsoleContext` as the desktop shell, so shared code in `features/` works on both. Its `nav.tabs` is an empty list, `keep` does nothing, and `close` goes back.

Back uses the browser history. Each pushed screen stores its `depth` in the history `state`. If the depth is above 0, Back calls `navigate(-1)`. If the stack started at this screen (a deep link or a push notification), Back replaces the entry with the workspace overview. `open(id, { push: true })` forces a new history entry for the same id, so Back closes a sub-page. The mobile shell has no keyboard shortcuts. It keeps the theme in component state and not in the saved layout.

## API client

`api/client.ts` exports `httpApi`, one function for each REST route, and the type `Api = typeof httpApi`. Every function builds its path with `encodeURIComponent` and calls the private `request<T>(method, path, body, signal)`.

The routes group as follows. [Server, REST API, and WebSocket](server-and-api.md) describes each route.

| Group | Functions |
| --- | --- |
| Sign-in | `info`, `exchange`, `signIns`, `revokeSignIn`, `revokeOtherSignIns`, `signOut` |
| Workspaces and settings | `workspaces`, `createWorkspace`, `workspace`, `saveSettings`, `deleteWorkspace`, `fixSettings`, `validateSettings`, `approveCommands`, `uiState`, `patchUiState` |
| MCP | `mcpStatus`, `mcpRefresh`, `mcpLogin`, `mcpLogout` |
| Projects and git | `importProject`, `cloneProject`, `pullProject`, `removeProject`, `initProject`, `git*`, and the git credential functions |
| Sessions and gates | `sessions`, `createSession`, `session`, `events`, `setYolo`, `amend`, `stopSession`, `pauseSession`, `resumeSession`, `uploadFile`, `answerGate`, `overrideDecision` |
| Executions | `execution`, `activity`, `cancelExecution`, `resumeExecution`, `inspectExecution` |
| Content | `artifact`, `diff`, `lessons`, `skills`, `books`, `cost`, `ask`, and the artifact upload, move, hide, and delete functions |
| Files and code | `projectTree`, `projectFile`, `saveProjectFile`, `projectFiles`, `projectDiff`, `projectChanges`, and the `code*` functions |
| Navigation | `tree`, `search`, `workspaceActivity` |
| Setup | `environment`, `saveProvider`, `onboarding`, `completeOnboarding`, `harnessSetup`, `listDir`, `fsBrowse`, `fsMkdir` |

### What happens when a request fails

- **Status 401:** `request` calls every `onUnauthorized` listener, then still throws. `App` shows `SignIn`.
- **Any other non-2xx status:** `request` throws `HttpError` with `status`, `message`, and `issues`. The message is the `error` field of the JSON body. When the body is not JSON, the message is the line `<status> <statusText>`. `issues` is the `issues` array of the body. A 422 from a settings or project form carries one `ValidationIssue` for each bad field. The form shows each issue next to its field.
- **Status 204 or an empty body:** the function returns `undefined`.
- **Raw uploads:** `rawPost` (artifact upload) and `uploadFile` (session upload) send `application/octet-stream`. They throw the same errors, but `uploadFile` throws a plain `Error`.

The client sends `credentials: "same-origin"`, so the session cookie goes with each call. It never stores a token.

## Generated types

The Rust types in `ostra-core` are the single source of the wire shapes. Each type that the browser sees has `#[derive(TS)]` and `#[ts(export)]`. The `ts-rs` crate writes one `.ts` file for each type into `web/src/api/gen/`. The folder holds 332 files, and git tracks them.

- **Export folder.** `.cargo/config.toml` sets `TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR` to `web/src/api/gen` (relative to the repo root).
- **Large integers.** The same file sets `TS_RS_LARGE_INT = "number"`. Without it, `u64` and `i64` fields become `bigint`, and `JSON.parse` cannot make a `bigint`.
- **Regenerate.** Run `cargo test -p ostra-core export_bindings`. The doc comment of `crates/ostra-core/src/api.rs` names this command. Commit the changed files in `gen/`.
- **Do not edit `gen/` by hand.** The next export overwrites the change. Biome skips the folder (`!web/src/api/gen` in `biome.json`).

Three small files give the app one import point:

- `api/types.ts` re-exports most generated types with `export type *`.
- `api/nav.ts` re-exports the navigation shapes (`WorkspaceTree`, `TreeSession`, `SearchResults`, `WorkspaceActivity`) and the aliases `SearchHitKind` and `ArtifactWithHeadings`.
- `api/extra.ts` defines the two types that Rust does not generate: `PtyFrame` and `SocketState` (`connecting`, `open`, or `closed`).

If a Rust type changes and the bindings are stale, `npm run typecheck` fails in the screens that use the type. This is the intended check, because the compiler finds each place that the change reaches.

## WebSocket manager

`api/socket.ts` defines `SocketManager`. The function `socket()` returns the one shared instance and starts it on the first call. The manager connects to `ws(s)://<host>/ws`. It handles JSON text frames of `ServerMsg` and binary PTY frames.

### Channels

A component subscribes to a **channel**. The manager counts the handlers of each channel. It sends `{ type: "subscribe", channel }` when the first handler arrives and `unsubscribe` when the last one leaves.

| Channel | Messages routed to it by `channelsFor` |
| --- | --- |
| `session:<id>` | `session_event`, and `session_updated` for that session |
| `execution:<id>` | `execution_delta`, `execution_status` |
| `term:<execution>` | Binary PTY frames. `terminal(execution, handler)` subscribes to it. |
| `workspace:<id>` | `workspace_updated`, `session_updated`, `project_fs_changed`, `git_progress`, `tree_patch`, `activity` |
| `home` | `workspace_updated`, `session_updated`, `harness_status` |

The messages `subscribed` and `error` belong to no channel. Only `onAny` listeners receive them. No code in `web/src` registers an `onAny` listener, so the console takes no action on an `error` message. The server throttles some of these messages: `tree_patch` and `git_progress` at most 4 each second, and `activity` at most 2 each second (comments in `crates/ostra-core/src/api.rs`).

### Reconnect

- When the socket closes, the manager waits `min(10000, 500 * 2^attempts)` ms and connects again. The waits are 500 ms, 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, and then 10 s. A successful open resets `attempts` to 0.
- On each open, the manager sends `subscribe` again for every channel that still has handlers.
- After an open that is not the first one, every `onReconnect` listener runs. Screens and stores use it to fetch their REST snapshot again, because messages that arrived while the socket was closed are lost.
- `send` drops a message when the socket is not open. This is safe for `subscribe`, because the open handler sends all subscriptions again.

### What happens after a lagged error

The server sends the `error` message `lagged` when the socket falls behind its notice channel. The socket stays open, so no reconnect happens. The manager gives the message only to `onAny` listeners, and the web code has none. The web code therefore fetches its REST snapshot again only through `onReconnect` listeners, after a socket reconnect. A screen that missed notices keeps its old data until the next reconnect, a reload, or a new live message for the same data. [Server, REST API, and WebSocket](server-and-api.md) owns the rules for when the server sends `lagged`.

### Code hints and terminal input

`hint(type, request)` asks the server for completions, signature help, or a navigation jump (`code_complete`, `code_signature`, `code_navigate`). It adds a numeric `id` and waits for the reply with the same `id`. The promise resolves to `null` in these cases:

- The socket is closed when the call starts or while it waits.
- The server does not answer within 30 seconds (`HINT_TIMEOUT_MS`).
- A newer request of the same type replaces it. The server also cancels the older request.

The browser sends terminal keystrokes as `term_input` and size changes as `term_resize`. A binary PTY frame has this layout: byte 0 is the length `n` of the execution id, the next `n` bytes are the id, and the rest is raw terminal output. `decodePtyFrame` returns `null` for a frame that is too short.

## Shared stores and live data

Several components can show the same data. For example, the sidebar, the palette, and the status bar all read the Sessions tree. `SharedStore<T>` in `lib/store.ts` makes them share one fetch and one socket subscription for each key.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Component
  participant S as SharedStore
  participant A as api (REST)
  participant W as SocketManager
  C->>S: subscribe(key)
  S->>W: live() subscribes to workspace:<ws>
  S->>A: load(key)
  A-->>S: snapshot
  S-->>C: data
  W-->>S: tree_patch or session_updated
  S-->>C: feed.update() gives new data
  W-->>S: onReconnect
  S->>A: load(key) again
```

The rules of the store are:

- `useShared(store, key)` reads an entry with `useSyncExternalStore`. A `null` key reads nothing.
- The entry starts when the first listener subscribes. It stops after the last listener leaves and one `setTimeout(0)` passes. The delay lets a remount in the same tick (StrictMode, a tab switch) keep the subscription.
- The last value stays cached after the entry stops. A screen that returns renders at once and refreshes in the background.
- Each `load` has a generation number `gen`. The store drops a late answer from an older load.
- The store calls `load` again after every socket reconnect.

`lib/live.ts` defines the stores and the hooks that read them:

| Hook | Source and live updates |
| --- | --- |
| `useWorkspaceTree(ws)` | `api.tree`. `tree_patch` replaces one session node. `session_updated` updates a row and keeps its runs and artifacts. |
| `useSessionSummaries(ws)` | `api.sessions`. Carries `yolo`, which the tree does not. |
| `useActivity(ws)` | `api.workspaceActivity`. `activity` replaces the value. |
| `useFileIndex(ws, key)` | `api.projectFiles`. Reloads on `project_fs_changed` for the project, at most once each second. |
| `useProjectChanges(ws, key)` | `api.projectChanges`. Same reload rule. |
| `useProjectFsChanges(ws, key, cb)` | Calls `cb(paths)` for each `project_fs_changed` of the project. |
| `useWorkspaces()` | `api.workspaces`. Reloads on `home` messages, at most once each second. |
| `useSocketState()` | The state of the socket manager. |
| `useSearch(ws, q)` | `api.search`, debounced 100 ms. An empty query sends no request. |

Older screens use `lib/hooks.ts`. `useAsync(load, deps)` loads once. It reloads when `deps` change and when the socket reconnects. `useChannel(channel, handler)` subscribes for the life of the component. `useThrottled(fn, ms)` limits calls with a trailing call. The session screen shows the pattern. It loads `api.session` and `api.events`, then appends each `session_event` of the channel `session:<id>` to a `live` list. It refreshes the detail at most once every 400 ms.

The execution screen (`screens/execution/useExecution.ts`) folds deltas into entries with `applyDelta` from `lib/events.ts`. `applyDelta` ignores a delta whose `seq` is at or below `lastSeq`. A REST snapshot and the live stream can therefore overlap. Deltas that arrive before the snapshot wait in a buffer and apply after it. After a reconnect, the hook asks only for items after the last `seq`.

## Shortcuts

`lib/shortcuts.ts` holds the model, and `Shell` holds the single `keydown` listener. An **action** is one of 11 ids: `palette`, `dock`, `sidebar`, `files`, `next-tab`, `prev-tab`, `close-tab`, `new-task`, `settings`, `theme`, and `keyboard-lock`. A **stroke** is a key press written as `ctrl+alt+shift+meta+<key>`, with the modifiers in that order. A binding has one stroke or two strokes in sequence.

| Action | Default on a Mac | Default elsewhere |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `palette` | `⌘K` | `Ctrl+K` |
| `dock` | `⌘/` | `Ctrl+/` |
| `sidebar` | `⌘B` | `Ctrl+B` |
| `files` | `⇧⌘E` | `Ctrl+Shift+E` |
| `next-tab`, `prev-tab` | `Ctrl+Tab`, `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | same |
| `close-tab` | `⌘W` (reserved) | `Ctrl+W` (reserved) |
| `new-task`, `settings`, `theme`, `keyboard-lock` | not bound | not bound |

`strokeOf` builds the stroke from a key event. If Shift or Alt is held, or the character is outside ASCII, it uses the physical key (`event.code`). Alt+K types a different character on a Mac, and the physical key keeps the stroke stable.

### How one key press is handled

1. If the stroke types text (no Ctrl, Alt, or Meta, and not a function key) and focus is in an editable element, the shell ignores it. Editable means `input`, `textarea`, `select`, a content-editable element, `.monaco-editor`, or `.ex-xterm`. The exception is a pending first stroke of a sequence.
2. `matchStroke` checks the bindings. A first stroke of a two-stroke binding sets `pending` and waits. The second stroke must come within `SEQUENCE_MS` (1500 ms).
3. `matchStroke` returns a `Match` with `action`, `pending`, and `consume`. If `consume` is true, the shell calls `preventDefault`. Then, if `action` is not null, the shell runs the action. A first stroke of a two-stroke binding returns `consume: true` with `action: null`. The shell calls `preventDefault` and runs nothing. A stroke that matches no binding returns `consume: false`, and the shell does nothing.
4. Ctrl+W in a terminal goes to the terminal, because Ctrl+W deletes a word in a shell.

A **reserved** binding (`close-tab` by default) is active only when the browser passes its own combinations to the page. That is the case when the keyboard is locked or when Ostra runs as an installed app (`runningAsApp()`). Without this rule, the console claims a stroke that the browser takes first. A binding that the user sets is never reserved.

### User changes

The user edits shortcuts in Settings, tab `shortcuts` (`ShortcutsSection`). `conflicts()` finds an action with the same keys, or one whose first stroke equals the new binding. `reservedBy()` warns when the browser or the system probably takes the stroke first. A first stroke becomes a one-key binding when no second stroke follows within 1200 ms (`SECOND_STROKE_MS`).

Overrides are stored in `localStorage` key `ostra.shortcuts.<ws>` as `{ "v": 1, "bindings": ... }`. They stay in this browser and do not go to the server. `parseOverrides` drops each entry with an unknown action, more than 2 strokes, or an invalid stroke. If storage is unavailable, the change lives in memory until the page reloads. A change reaches other components through a `CustomEvent` and reaches other browser tabs through the `storage` event.

The keyboard lock (`lib/keyboardLock.ts`) needs the Keyboard Lock API, which Chromium has. `lock` enters fullscreen and calls `navigator.keyboard.lock()`. Leaving fullscreen releases it.

## Command palette

The palette (`shell/Palette.tsx`, model in `lib/palette.ts`) opens with the `palette` action. It wraps `CommandPalette` from the design system.

- **Empty query.** The rows come from data that the shell holds: sessions, executions, artifacts, and projects (`localItems`), without file rows, then the commands.
- **A query.** The palette calls `api.search(ws, q)` through `useSearch`. When the server answers, the palette shows its hits sorted by `score`, then the matching commands. Before the answer arrives, or if the request fails, the palette filters the local rows. After a failure, it also loads the file index of the Files project, so file names stay searchable.
- **Order.** Groups appear in this order: Sessions, Executions, Artifacts, Projects, Files, Lessons, Settings, Workspace, Actions. The list holds at most 200 result rows (`MAX_ROWS`) before the commands, because the palette renders every row.
- **Commands.** `New task`, `New workspace…`, `Add project…`, `Cost`, `Settings`, `Keyboard shortcuts`, `Ask a quick question`, and `Toggle light and dark theme`. The keyboard-lock command appears only when the browser supports the lock. Each row shows the user's shortcut as a hint.
- **Select.** `paletteTarget` maps an id. A `cmd:` id runs a shell command. A `lesson:` id opens `ws:memory` with the id as anchor. A `setting:` id opens `ws:settings` with the id as anchor. Any other id opens the resource.

## Mock API

The console runs without a server when `VITE_MOCK=1`. `api/index.ts` sets `isMock` and chooses the implementation:

```ts
export const isMock = import.meta.env.VITE_MOCK === "1";
export const api: Api = isMock ? (await import("./mock/mockApi")).mockApi : httpApi;
```

The import is dynamic on purpose. A static import keeps the fixtures in the production bundle even when the branch is dead. `socket.ts` does the same for `mockSocket`. Both mocks implement the same interfaces as the real code (`Api` and `SocketLike`), so the screens do not know which one they use.

- **`mockApi`** (`api/mock/mockApi.ts`) answers each call from fixtures after 80 ms. It keeps mutable state, so answers to gates, stops, settings, and skills stay until the page reloads. A thrown error becomes `HttpError(404, ...)`. The URL query `?first-run` shows the first-run setup.
- **`mockSocket`** opens after 50 ms. It streams the fixture deltas of running executions every 1800 ms (`STEP_MS`) on `execution:<id>`. It sends the terminal backlog and live chunks on `term:<id>`, and it echoes `term_input`. Under vitest (`MODE === "test"`) it never opens, so tests have no timers.
- **Modes.** `npm run dev:mock` runs `vite --mode mock`, and `web/.env.mock` sets `VITE_MOCK=1`. Vitest sets the same variable in `vite.config.ts`.
- **Shot mode.** `web/.env.shot` sets `VITE_SHOT=1` and `VITE_MOCK=1`. This build is the console that the homepage of the project shows in an iframe. It uses a memory router that starts at the `?path=` of the iframe, limited to `/w/` routes. The page sends messages of type `ostra-shot` to the console. The console sends `ostra-shot-ready`, `ostra-shot-nav`, and `ostra-shot-theme` to the parent page (`web/src/shell/shot.ts`, `useShotBridge`). The console accepts a message only from the parent window and the same origin. A Vite plugin (`shotCsp`) writes a `Content-Security-Policy` meta tag into the page, because a static host cannot send the header that the server sends.

Keep the fixtures in step with the generated types. A fixture that does not match a type fails `npm run typecheck`.

## Browser features outside the shell

- **Theme.** `lib/theme.ts` sets `data-theme` on `<html>`. `resolveTheme` uses a stored `light` or `dark`, or the system setting, and falls back to `dark`. Pages outside a workspace read `localStorage` key `ostra.theme`.
- **Install.** `lib/install.ts` captures `beforeinstallprompt` so Settings can offer an install button. `InstallState` is `installed`, `ready`, or `manual`. For `manual`, `manualInstallHint()` returns steps for Safari and Firefox, or a note that the page needs HTTPS or localhost.
- **Web Push.** `lib/push.ts` registers `/sw.js`. `enablePush()` asks for permission, reads `vapid_public_key` from `api.info()`, subscribes with `userVisibleOnly`, and sends the subscription with `api.pushSubscribe`. It returns a message when the browser lacks support, the user blocks notifications, or the server has no key. `web/public/sw.js` shows each push and opens its `url` on click. The sender belongs to [MCP servers and Web Push](mcp-and-notifications.md).
- **Markdown.** `components/Markdown.tsx` renders agent-written text with `react-markdown` and `remark-gfm`. It does not render raw HTML. It keeps an image only when its source starts with `data:image/`. A remote image requests a URL that the agent chose, so this rule backs up the CSP of the server.

## Build and embedding

`npm run build` in `web/` runs `vite build` and writes `web/dist`. A release build of the `ostra` binary embeds that folder with `rust_embed` (`#[folder = "../../web/dist"]` in `crates/ostra-server/src/assets.rs`). The embed rule is in [Server, REST API, and WebSocket](server-and-api.md). The folder is not in git (`web/dist` is in `.gitignore`).

Run `npm run build` in `web/` before `cargo build --release -p ostra-server`. If `web/dist` is missing or old, the release binary embeds a missing or old UI. If the embedded folder has no `index.html`, the server answers 200 with the text "The web build is missing. Run `npm run build` in web/ and rebuild ostra."

### Build settings

- **Output.** `outDir` is `dist`, with `emptyOutDir` and no source maps.
- **Chunks.** `vite.config.ts` puts `react` (with `react-dom` and `scheduler`), `react-router`, `lucide-react`, and `react-markdown` (with `remark-gfm`) into named chunks. They change less often than the app, so a UI change keeps them in the browser cache. Monaco and xterm stay in their own lazy chunks. `chunkSizeWarningLimit` is 4000 KB because of Monaco.
- **Scripts.** `build.sh` runs `npm ci` when `node_modules` is missing. It rebuilds `web/dist` when a file in `web/src`, `web/public`, `web/index.html`, `web/package.json`, `design/src`, or `design/package.json` is newer than `web/dist/index.html`. Then it runs `cargo build --release -p ostra-server`. The `Dockerfile` builds the `web` stage first and copies `web/dist` into the Rust stage. See [Install, run, and the command line](install-and-run.md).

### How the server serves the build

`static_handler` in `assets.rs` follows these rules:

- A path under `assets/` gets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, because the file name holds a content hash. Every other file gets `no-cache`.
- An unknown path returns `index.html`, so a client route such as `/w/ws_1/f/app/src/main.rs` loads the app.
- A path that starts with `api/`, `internal/`, or `assets/` returns 404. A root-level file name with a dot that is not `.html` also returns 404, for example a missing `/favicon.ico`. A missing asset must not return HTML.
- `sw.js` sits at the root, so the service worker covers the whole app.

The server adds a `Content-Security-Policy` header to responses (`secure_headers` in `crates/ostra-server/src/api.rs`). It allows scripts, workers, and the manifest only from the same origin. It allows images only from the same origin and `data:`. It allows WebSocket connections to the request host. The console therefore cannot load a remote script or image.

### Dev server

`npm run dev` starts Vite on port 5173. It proxies `/api`, `/ws` (as a WebSocket), and `/mcp/oauth` to `OSTRA_DEV_SERVER`. The default is `http://127.0.0.1:7878`, the default Ostra port. The OAuth redirect for MCP servers returns to the origin of the page, which is why `/mcp/oauth` is proxied. Run `ostra serve` first, and sign in with the printed link. The design gallery is at `/_design` in dev only.

## Commands

Run these in `web/`. `package.json` defines them.

| Command | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Vite dev server against a real `ostra`. |
| `npm run dev:mock` | Vite dev server with fixtures and no server. |
| `npm run build` | Production build into `web/dist`. |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`. TypeScript runs in strict mode with `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters`. |
| `npm test` | `vitest run` in the `jsdom` environment with `VITE_MOCK=1`. It runs `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*.test.tsx`. |
| `npm run check` | Biome lint and format check. `check:fix` writes the fixes. |

The tests render the real `routes` with `createMemoryRouter` and the mock API. For example, `App.test.tsx` and `shell/WorkspaceShell.test.tsx` open a path and read the tab strip. Biome uses 2 spaces, a line width of 120, double quotes, and trailing commas.

## What happens when

- **The server returns 401.** `App` shows `SignIn`. After a good exchange, the page reloads at `/`.
- **The socket drops.** The status bar shows `Offline, reconnecting`. The manager retries with the backoff above. After it reconnects, stores and `useAsync` reload their snapshots.
- **The server sends a `lagged` error.** The socket stays open and no reconnect happens. The web code takes no action, and no snapshot reloads.
- **A URL names an unknown resource.** `RouteScreen` shows "Nothing here." and the workspace overview stays one click away.
- **The workspace folder is gone.** `api.workspace` fails. The shell shows `Workspace not available` and a button to the workspace list.
- **The window shrinks below 721 px.** `useIsMobile()` turns true and `WorkspaceShell` swaps `Shell` for `MobileShell`. The desktop shell loses its local tab state, but the saved layout stays.
- **Two browser tabs change shortcuts.** The `storage` event updates the other tab.
- **Local storage is unavailable.** Layout, theme, panel widths, and shortcuts keep working in memory for the page. They reset on reload, and the layout can still come from the server copy.
- **A search request fails.** The palette uses local rows and the file index.
- **A hint request goes stale.** The code editor receives `null` and shows no popup.

## Rules for a change

- Add a screen in `screens/`, add a case to `ScreenFor`, and add the id to `lib/resource.ts` and to `resourceFromPath`. Add a `selfScrolling` entry if the screen scrolls itself.
- Add a mobile case in `MobileScreenFor` for each new resource type.
- Open resources with `useNav().open`. Do not call `navigate` in a screen.
- Read shared data with a `lib/live.ts` hook. Add a `SharedStore` when two components need the same data.
- Add a REST function to `httpApi` and a matching one to `mockApi`. The `Api` type makes the compiler check both.
- After a Rust type change, run `cargo test -p ostra-core export_bindings` and commit `web/src/api/gen`.
- Import Monaco and xterm only through `lazy()`.
